papers.title: PmiREN3.0: a multi-omics integrated and AI-assisted encyclopedia for plant microRNA research.
papers.abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are key post-transcriptional regulators in gene regulatory networks (GRNs). Comprehensive research on miRNAs increasingly requires the integration of large and heterogeneous datasets, together with more efficient approaches to knowledge exploration. Here, we present PmiREN3.0, a major update of the Plant MicroRNA Encyclopedia. Compared with PmiREN2.0, species/subspecies coverage increased from 179 to 340, adding 22 orders, 51 families, and 108 genera. Using the same standardized workflow and annotation criteria as previous releases, high-confidence miRNAs were identified from 5319 small RNA sequencing (sRNA-seq) datasets, with miRNA loci increasing from 39 751 to 87 667 and miRNA families from 7838 to 18 389. Resources and tools from previous releases were extensively updated, while six new modules were added for primary transcripts, DNA methylation, RNA modifications, stress-responsive expression, metabolic pathways, and core GRNs. PmiREN3.0 also introduces miRai+, a knowledge service powered by artificial intelligence (AI) that combines a language model fine-tuned on miRNA knowledge with retrieval augmented generation. Evaluation yielded scores of 0.910 for answer relevance, 0.965 for faithfulness, and 0.906 for factual correctness. Together, PmiREN3.0 provides an expanded plant miRNA dataset and an integrated platform combining multi-omics data and AI-assisted knowledge services for plant miRNA research. PmiREN3.0 is available at https://pmiren.com/.

papers.title: Simpler is not always better: Phylodynamic misspecification and deep-learning corrections.
papers.abstract: Phylodynamics bridges the gap between epidemiology and pathogen genetic data. The birth-death (BD) model and its extensions serve to infer the average number of secondary infections Re and the infection duration d from time-scaled pathogen phylogenies. Moreover, more complex models add extra parameters, such as the average length of the incubation period, the proportion of superspreaders in the infected population, or the speed-up in detection after contact-tracing. However, these additional parameters come at an important computational cost: While the simplest, BD, model, has a closed-form solution, its extensions do not and require numerical methods for their likelihood computation. This leads to increased computational times and potential numerical errors. Therefore, the BD model remains the favorite researchers'choice for real dataset analyses, and is often applied even in cases where more complex epidemiological aspects are present. We investigated, using simulations, how model misspecification influences inference of Re and d in the phylodynamic framework. We showed that the use of models not accounting for various epidemiological aspects leads to bias. In particular the simplest, BD, estimator tends to underestimate Re in the presence of super-spreading, incubation or contact-tracing, which might be dangerous from the public health perspective. In contrast, deep-learning-based estimators for complex models, accounting for multiple epidemiological factors, performed well in our simulations both on the data where those factors were present and where they were absent. This motivates the use of complex epidemiologically realistic estimators, whose design has recently become possible thanks to deep learning.

papers.title: Advances in assessing donor organ quality and perioperative risk for kidney transplantation.
papers.abstract: Kidney transplantation faces persistent challenges in accurately evaluating donor organ quality and predicting long-term outcomes, with traditional assessment methods demonstrating limited predictive capacity. The increasing utilization of marginal-quality donor organs has intensified the need for sophisticated evaluation strategies. Machine perfusion technology has transformed organ preservation from mere static storage to a dynamic platform potentially enabling real-time monitoring, assessment, and interventions during the preservation period. Molecular profiling technologies such as genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics could provide refined biomarkers for donor kidney assessment across several phases of kidney transplantation. The first window arises during donor evaluation. Techniques such as high-resolution molecular typing, genetic profiling, epigenomic markers, and artificial intelligence-enhanced imaging provide additional information compared to traditional scoring systems. During organ preservation, a second window emerges, allowing additional, isolated assessment of the organ after procurement but before transplantation. Machine perfusion systems enable sampling of perfusate and tissue for multi-omics analysis to characterize injury or function, although most candidate biomarkers remain at the discovery or early validation stage. After transplantation, donor-derived cell-free deoxyribonucleic acid, urinary chemokines, and advanced imaging modalities offer non-invasive early detection of graft injury. Clinical translation of these new techniques faces substantial challenges: most studies are single-center and have small sample sizes, assay standardization remains incomplete, and evidence linking biomarker-guided decisions to improved long-term graft survival is lacking. Machine learning may enhance risk stratification but remains largely unvalidated in prospective trials. Future progress requires a shift from short-term endpoint prediction to long-term outcome validation through multicenter studies, standardized protocols, and equitable implementation strategies.

papers.title: Future directions and challenges of drug development and non-human primate models.
papers.abstract: Gene and cell therapy are transforming therapeutic approaches for genetic diseases and malignancies. This review examines the current role and future directions of non-human primate (NHP) models in preclinical safety evaluation of adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapy and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy amid accelerating adoption of new approach methodologies (NAMs). We systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure for publications from January 2015 to June 2026; approximately 60 English-language and 5 Chinese-language publications, together with FDA, EMA, and NMPA guidance documents, were included. NHPs remain the reference species for AAV and CAR-T safety evaluation, yet supply crises, ethical pressures, and documented prediction gaps (hepatotoxicity, dorsal root ganglion injury) are driving NAMs adoption. Organoids, organs-on-chips (87% sensitivity and 100% specificity for drug-induced liver injury), and AI-driven models are maturing under the FDA Modernization Act 2.0 and the 2025 FDA roadmap. We propose the Hierarchical Replacement Assessment Framework (HRAF), a three-tier, two-threshold model that reallocates NHP resources from routine screening to risk confirmation, providing an actionable roadmap for mechanism-based and welfare-conscious preclinical development.

papers.title: Structural Diversity and Functional Roles of the Internalin Family Proteins in Listeria monocytogenes.
papers.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes is an important foodborne intracellular pathogen that can cause listeriosis in humans and animals, with a relatively high mortality rate. Internalin (Inl) family proteins are critical virulence factors of L. monocytogenes and play essential roles in bacterial adhesion, host cell invasion, tissue colonization, immune evasion, and systemic infection. In recent years, with the continuous advancement of genomics, structural biology, and host-pathogen interaction studies, an increasing number of internalin family members and their biological functions have been identified. Different internalins exhibit significant differences in receptor recognition, tissue tropism, and pathogenic mechanisms. This review systematically summarizes the structural characteristics and classification of the internalin family in L. monocytogenes, with particular emphasis on recent advances in the functions of major family members, including InlA, InlB, InlC, InlK, InlF, InlP, InlL, and InlJ, in intestinal invasion, penetration of the placental and blood-brain barriers, intracellular survival, immune evasion, biofilm formation, and host interactions. Furthermore, recent research hotspots in the functional characterization of internalin proteins are discussed, along with their potential applications in elucidating virulence mechanisms, vaccine development, and targeted prevention and control strategies. This review aims to provide a theoretical reference for further investigations into the pathogenic mechanisms of L. monocytogenes and the development of novel prevention and control strategies.

papers.title: BioDecryptors, a Bioinformatics Escape Game for Undergraduate and Postgraduate Learners in Clinical Microbiology: Prospective Before-and-After Study.
papers.abstract: Bioinformatics is increasingly important in clinical microbiology with growing use of genomic sequencing, metagenomics, and phylogenetic analyses. However, introducing bioinformatics concepts and tools to medical learners can be challenging. Gamified educational approaches may allow introducing these concepts while supporting learner motivation. This study prospectively evaluated BioDecryptors, an educational escape game to introduce bioinformatics principles and tools in clinical microbiology, by assessing short-term changes in knowledge and self-reported motivation and evaluating participant satisfaction. We conducted a prospective before-and-after study between January and September 2025. Volunteers were recruited from undergraduate medical programs at Université Paris Cité and postgraduate programs or training activities for MDs and PharmDs at Université de Nantes, Université Paris-Saclay, and the French Society for Microbiology. Overall, 55 participants were included: 22 (40%) second-year medical students and 33 (60%) postgraduate MDs or PharmDs. Participants completed BioDecryptors in teams of 3 to 4 using versions adapted to their training level. Knowledge was assessed before and immediately after the activity using 2 distinct 10-item tests assessing the same predefined learning objectives. Motivation was assessed using a 12-item, 5-point Likert questionnaire covering 3 predefined domains, and satisfaction was assessed after the activity. Pre-post knowledge scores were compared using paired t tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, as appropriate. Motivation items were analyzed using paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Statistical significance was defined as a 2-sided P <.05. Paired knowledge assessments were available for 50 participants. Mean knowledge scores increased from 7.0 (SD 2.0; 95% CI 6.4-7.5) before the activity to 7.9 (SD 2.0; 95% CI 7.4-8.5) afterward ( P <.001). The mean change was 0.93 (SD 1.39; 95% CI 0.26-1.60) points among undergraduates and 0.83 (SD 1.21; 95% CI 0.38-1.27) points among postgraduates, with no statistically significant between-group difference ( P =.79). Motivation increased for perceived usefulness ( P =.04), willingness to learn ( P =.01), understanding of bioinformatics in diseases ( P =.002), and confidence in bioinformatics abilities ( P =.002). Curiosity ( P =.46) and interest in real-life applications ( P =.33) did not significantly change. Among 50 satisfaction respondents, overall satisfaction was high (mean 4.7, SD 0.5; 95% CI 4.6-4.9); 98% (48/49) of the respondents to the corresponding item indicated an interest in other escape game modules. Participation in BioDecryptors was associated with short-term increases in bioinformatics knowledge and self-reported motivation, together with high participant satisfaction. Unlike previously reported escape games focusing primarily on clinical or infection-control topics, BioDecryptors integrates hands-on bioinformatics analyses into a clinical microbiology scenario and offers versions adapted to undergraduate and postgraduate learners. Our findings provide preliminary evidence supporting the feasibility and acceptability of this approach as a complementary educational resource for introducing bioinformatics in health professions training. Controlled studies with longer-term assessments are needed to establish its comparative educational effectiveness and knowledge retention.

papers.title: Nitroxoline treatment of Balamuthia mandrillaris triggers genomic crisis, transcriptional collapse, and incomplete encystment via copper and iron chelation.
papers.abstract: Balamuthia mandrillaris is a free-living amoeba that can infect the central nervous system to cause granulomatous amebic encephalitis (GAE), a fatal disease with mortality rates up to 90%. GAE is typically treated with a six-drug regimen with limited efficacy and significant toxicity. Our lab previously identified nitroxoline, a quinolone antibiotic, as a promising therapeutic complement to the existing regimen, and in 2021 nitroxoline was first successfully used to treat a human patient. In this study, we elucidate nitroxoline's mechanism of action using a combination of genomics, transcriptomics, chemical complementation, growth assays, and electron microscopy. In service of this goal, an annotated draft genome of B. mandrillaris strain CDC:V039 was generated using long read sequencing, yielding over 32,000 predicted protein coding sequences, the majority of which were present on telomere-to-telomere predicted chromosomal contigs. Leveraging this resource, comparative transcriptomics were used to characterize encystment responses to three different cellular stressors: nitroxoline, galactose, and hypoxia. Our findings reveal that nitroxoline-induced cysts undergo transcriptional collapse and genomic and structural destabilization via copper and iron chelation, and that preformed cysts are also disrupted by nitroxoline. These data provide insight into nitroxoline's multifaceted impact on B. mandrillaris growth and cellular processes and advance our understanding of the transcriptional landscape associated with stress induced encystment. Our findings support the continued clinical study of nitroxoline as a complement to the existing regimen.

papers.title: Novel Biomarkers for Bacterial Meningitis and Other Central Nervous System Infections.
papers.abstract: Timely and accurate diagnosis of central nervous system (CNS) infections remains challenging because of nonspecific clinical characteristics and limited diagnostic accuracy of conventional tests. Novel cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers may improve early diagnosis and facilitate differentiation between infectious aetiologies. This review summarizes established and emerging CSF biomarkers for the diagnosis of CNS infections, with a focus on bacterial meningitis, and discusses their potential clinical application. Several novel CSF biomarkers have demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance for bacterial meningitis. Among these, CSF C-reactive protein (CRP) has recently been implemented in clinical practice, while heparin-binding protein and combinations of CSF CRP with inflammatory cytokines such as IL-6 and IL-1β show similarly high diagnostic accuracy. Pathogen-specific biomarkers, including CXCL13 for neuroborreliosis and β-D-glucan and galactomannan for fungal CNS infections, further expand the diagnostic repertoire. In addition, multi-omics approaches, including metabolomics, lipidomics, and proteomics, have identified promising candidates such as pyruvate and phosphatidylcholines, although these require further validation. Untargeted techniques, including metagenomic next-generation sequencing and phage immunoprecipitation sequencing, further enhance pathogen detection and may complement microbiological testing. Novel biomarkers have the potential to substantially improve the diagnosis of CNS infections. Several biomarkers for bacterial meningitis are already available for clinical implementation, particularly in patients with intermediate CSF leukocyte counts, where diagnostic uncertainty is greatest. For viral and other CNS infections biomarkers remain scarce. Future studies should focus on validation of emerging biomarkers and on integrating biomarker panels with advanced molecular diagnostic techniques to enable rapid, accurate and clinically applicable diagnostic strategies.

papers.title: Comparative genomics and machine learning reveal antimicrobial resistance landscapes, population structures, and geographic signatures of pork-associated Salmonella Derby across major producing countries.
papers.abstract: Salmonella Derby is a major pork-associated foodborne pathogen, yet its genomic diversity across pork-producing countries has not been systematically compared. This study aimed to compare antimicrobial resistance (AMR) landscapes, population structures, and geographic genomic signatures. We analyzed all publicly available pork-associated genomes in the National Center for Biotechnology Information Pathogen Detection database (January 2025) from China (n = 235), France (n = 83), Mexico (n = 38), and the United States (n = 109), using co-occurrence and pairwise association analyses, core-genome phylogeny, and a random forest classifier trained on pan-genome gene presence/absence. Chinese isolates carried the most AMR determinants (15.3 per isolate), followed by Mexican (7.6), French (3.5), and American (3.0) isolates; this difference, and most country-associated AMR genes (ARGs), persisted within sequence type 40 (ST40). Moreover, fosA7.3 and tet(A) were hub ARGs in all countries, and in France ARG and virulence gene profiles were almost perfectly partitioned between ST39 and ST40. Phylogenetic analysis resolved two clades separated by 37,107-38,674 core-genome single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs); the dominant subclade was overwhelmingly ST40. One American ST40 isolate differed by only 18-20 SNPs from three French ST40 isolates. The classifier discriminated country with accuracy of 0.93-0.99 across 21 training:testing splits, remaining ≥ 0.96 when closely related isolates (≤ 10 SNPs) were kept in the same partition; an unannotated gene cluster (group 52) and the efflux pump gene acrF were the most informative features. These findings show strong country-level genomic structuring in pork-associated S. Derby, with implications for global surveillance and source attribution.

papers.title: Nationwide clinical-genomic epidemiology of listeriosis in Taiwan, 2018-2025: disease manifestations in relation to clonal background.
papers.abstract: Listeriosis is an uncommon but severe foodborne infection, yet nationwide data linking pathogen genomics with clinical manifestations remain limited. We analyzed 1,252 laboratory-confirmed symptomatic listeriosis cases reported through nationwide surveillance in Taiwan during 2018-2025, with whole-genome sequencing of the corresponding clinical Listeria monocytogenes isolate from every case. The average annual incidence was 6.68 cases per 1,000,000 person-years, and 30-day all-cause mortality was 11.4%. Incidence showed an age-dependent sex pattern, with higher incidence among females aged 15-44 years and a shift toward male predominance at older ages. The female excess at ages 15-44 years persisted after exclusion of documented maternal-neonatal cases (male-to-female incidence rate ratio, 0.57; 95% confidence interval, 0.36-0.89). Clonal complex 87 (CC87) was the predominant CC (35.9%), whereas CC1 and CC2 were associated with higher odds of central nervous system (CNS) infection. LIPI-4 occurred predominantly in CC87, and LIPI-4-positive isolates showed lower odds of CNS infection; however, this association could not be separated from clonal background. More broadly, most associations of pathogenicity islands, virulence genes, and their alleles with disease manifestations could not be separated from the underlying clonal backgrounds in which these markers occurred, and none of the estimable associations remained significant after CC adjustment. This nationwide clinical-genomic study characterizes the contemporary burden of listeriosis in Taiwan and highlights clonal background as essential context for interpreting associations between virulence markers and disease manifestations.

papers.title: Seasonal variation in chytrid infection in a stream-dwelling frog in Southern Brazil.
papers.abstract: Many wildlife disease systems exhibit pronounced seasonal dynamics driven by environmental conditions that modulate pathogen growth and host susceptibility. The aquatic fungus Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd), which infects and threatens amphibians worldwide, presents a seasonal infection pattern linked to different factors that drive disease outbreaks and population decline. Here, we investigated seasonal and individual variation in Bd infection in the stream-dwelling frog Limnomedusa macroglossa, which inhabits rocky outcrops in southern Brazil. A seasonal infection peak was detected, with higher prevalence and infection loads during the cold months, and temperature was an important predictor of Bd detection probability. Individuals that exhibited infection peaks during the cold season showed a marked reduction or complete clearance of Bd when recaptured in the warm season, and many remained Bd-negative or maintained very low loads, suggesting rapid infection clearance. These findings indicate that the analyzed population can persist despite the presence of the aquatic pathogen. Identifying the microclimatic factors that enable hosts to eliminate Bd infections, or alternatively, promote pathogen persistence in the environment, is crucial for understanding population resilience and informing wildlife disease management strategies.

papers.title: Infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus detection system established based on the multienzyme isothermal rapid amplification (MIRA) method.
papers.abstract: Infectious hematopoietic necrosis virus (IHNV) is an important pathogen of salmonid fish. In this study, a multienzyme isothermal rapid amplification (MIRA) assay targeting a conserved region of the IHNV N gene was established for rapid detection. The performance of the assay was evaluated using IHNV RNA standards, and further compared with digital PCR (dPCR) using 8 IHNV isolates, 12 cell culture supernatants, and 67 tissue samples from rainbow trout suspected of IHNV infection. The MIRA assay produced detectable signals within approximately 20 min. A detection rate of 100% was achieved at 102 copies μl-1 using RNA standards. The assay successfully detected all 8 IHNV isolates and showed no cross-reaction with non-target fish viruses. For cell culture supernatants and tissue samples, the MIRA assay showed a high level of agreement with dPCR results. These findings indicate that the MIRA assay may serve as a rapid and practical method for IHNV detection, particularly for on-site screening and preliminary diagnosis in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Air pollution is associated with a distinct pathogen spectrum in community-acquired pneumonia: a prospective multicentre cohort study.
papers.abstract: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) is the leading cause of death due to infection worldwide, with its incidence and disease course influenced by air pollution exposure. Little is known about how air pollution influences microbiological findings in patients with CAP. Patients were recruited from a prospective, multicentre study of CAP (CAPNETZ). Air pollution data were collected at the city level considering data up to one month before inclusion. Associations with sputum pathogen detection and cell counts were tested using generalised linear mixed-effects logistic regression models adjusting for clinical confounders, centre-level heterogeneity and meteorological data. Internal validation was performed using an Ensemble Feature Selection (EFS) approach. Among 4,446 eligible patients with available sputum samples, a potential pathogen was detected in 1,581 patients, while complete sputum-cell-count data were available for 4,014 patients. Detection of Streptococcus pneumoniae was associated with previous higher exposure to sulphur dioxide (SO 2 ) (OR 1.75, p = 0.008) and carbon monoxide (CO) (OR 1.57, p = 0.02). Escherichia coli was more frequently detected in patients who were exposed to elevated levels of nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) (OR 2.75, p = 0.004) and higher temperature (OR 1.51, p = 0.03), whereas increased fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) exposure (OR 0.37, p = 0.001) was linked to reduced detection. Furthermore, SO 2 exposure influenced the likelihood of obtaining a diagnostically relevant sputum culture and was associated with higher odds of detecting a high leucocyte count (OR 1.18, p = 0.02). Results were largely corroborated by EFS, particularly for S. pneumoniae and E. coli detection. Exposure to air pollution was associated with a distinct pathogen spectrum in patients with CAP. These findings may have implications for the interpretation of microbiological data in an epidemiological and clinical context and highlight the importance of considering air pollution exposure as a confounding factor. Further validation in cohorts with high-quality environmental, microbiological and antimicrobial resistance data is needed. Registry: German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS), DRKS-ID: DRKS00005274, Registration date: 2013-09-11.

papers.title: Site-specific outcomes and genomics in metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Clinical and molecular features of pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) according to involved metastatic sites have not been well characterized. We used the Foundry platform to query information for patients with metastatic PDAC at MD Anderson Cancer Center. Involved metastatic sites were extracted using natural language processing from imaging reports and verified by chart reviews. Overall survival (OS) and next-generation sequencing (NGS) data were analyzed. In a cohort of 1095 patients (median overall survival [OS]: 22.8 months), lung-only metastasis was associated with longer median OS (57.6 months, P < .0001). Patients with metastases not involving the liver had OS of 41.3 months, while liver-only (19.5 months) and multiple sites including liver (19.3 months) had the poorest survival. TP53 mutation rates were higher in liver-involved groups (84-85%) vs lung-only (73%) and non-liver metastases (67%, P < .0001). Lower rates of GNAS mutations were detected in liver-only (5%) and liver-involved (2%) cases, and higher in lung-only (8%) and non-liver (10%, P < .01). The frequency of KRAS mutation and mutant allele distribution were not significantly different in tissue-based NGS. However, in liquid biopsy analysis (n = 240), lung-only metastasis showed the lowest mutation detection (50%), TP53 (23%) and KRAS (10%), compared to liver-only detection rates of 65%, 46%, and 52%, respectively (P values: .009, .02, <.001). Patients with PDAC without liver metastasis have significantly improved OS and lower rates of TP53 mutation. Patients with lung-only metastasis had longer OS, a lower liquid-biopsy positivity rate, and a lower rate of KRAS detection by liquid biopsy; because liquid biopsy may under-detect KRAS in lung-only disease, tumor-tissue sequencing should be prioritized in these patients as KRAS-directed therapies emerge.

papers.title: Single-cell CRISPR screen maps epigenetic regulators of lineage specification and malignancies in human HSPCs.
papers.abstract: Mapping how genetic perturbations influence cell fate is key to understanding human development and disease. Here, we developed a massively parallel single-cell CRISPR (scCRISPR) screening platform in primary human hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), profiling 322 regulators across 172,382 single-perturbed cells. The resulting multi-layered regulatory framework captured known associations and enabled functional annotation of regulator-phenotype relationships. Specifically, our atlas revealed that regulators acted within perturbation clusters to govern distinct gene programs that shaped cell fate. As proof of concept, we illustrated several examples. SMYD3 emerged as a negative regulator of long-term regenerative capacity. Analysis of lineage output further identified KMT5B, TRIM24, SETD7, and NSD3 as regulators associated with lineage-biased outputs. Finally, integration with clinical datasets identified PRDM10 as a candidate dependency in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). This work establishes a scalable functional genomics platform in a primary human stem cell system.

papers.title: Integrating clinical diagnostics with interventional genetics for neurodevelopmental disorders.
papers.abstract: Interventional genetics (IG) refers to the development of therapies aimed at treating the underlying genetic cause of disease. Diagnostic sequencing has advanced to the point where genetic results can be returned within weeks, meaning that therapeutically actionable variants associated with specific diseases could be developed immediately after diagnosis. Here, we describe 81 probands with a neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD) and family matched controls with full genotype/phenotype information and biobanked stem cells, most of which are consented for sharing. We outline a rapid and scalable pipeline for induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) generation directly from clinical collection, without the need for peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) storage, paired with induction to neurons. We provide a proof of principle for rapid creation of oligonucleotide therapeutics for Kleefstra syndrome. This work introduces a cohort of individuals with NDDs and an implemental pipeline to integrate IG with clinical diagnostics for NDDs. This information documents our experience and provides useful details for clinical centers interested in integrating IG for NDDs with diagnostic sequencing.

papers.title: Identification of CD40 as the target of artemisinin via targeted degradomics for ulcerative colitis.
papers.abstract: Current drugs for ulcerative colitis often face challenges such as significant side effects, high costs, and tendency to induce drug resistance. Repurposing existing drugs is a promising approach that builds on their known safety and efficacy profiles. Artemisinin (Art), a first-line antimalarial agent, shows anti-inflammatory activity. Malaria infection is frequently accompanied by severe intestinal inflammation and barrier disruption, pathological features that share similarities with ulcerative colitis. However, Art's precise anti-inflammatory mechanism and its therapeutic efficacy in ulcerative colitis remain unclear. In this study, using a DSS-induced ulcerative colitis mouse model, we confirmed that Art significantly ameliorates colitis symptoms and restores intestinal barrier function. Mechanistically, we used PROTAC-based targeted degradomics and identified the immunomodulatory protein CD40 as a candidate target of Art. Art treatment was associated with reduced CD40-TRAF6 interaction, suppression of downstream NF-κB and MAPK inflammatory signaling, and decreased release of inflammatory cytokines. This study provides a novel drug candidate and mechanistic foundation for the application of Art in the treatment of ulcerative colitis.

papers.title: Genetic data sharing by clinical laboratories in Canada: A position statement by the Canadian College of Medical Geneticists.
papers.abstract: Next-generation sequencing has transformed diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment across rare disease, cancer, immunology, and infectious disease. As variant interpretation may evolve with emerging evidence, sharing genetic data is essential to improve diagnostic accuracy and advance genomic medicine. However, practical guidance for implementing clinical genetic data sharing remains limited. The Canadian College of Medical Geneticists (CCMG), therefore, developed national guidance to support secure, ethical, and effective genetic data sharing by Canadian clinical laboratories. An ad hoc CCMG working group with broad geographic and disciplinary representation developed the initial framework of this guidance through six meetings. Members included clinical laboratory geneticists, genomics specialists, a legal expert, a clinical geneticist, and a genetic counselor. The process drew on expert consensus (including patient and family perspectives), existing frameworks, and relevant peer-reviewed evidence, followed by iterative external review. Reporting was informed by the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation II (AGREE II) framework. The guidance provides recommendations to support genetic data sharing by Canadian clinical laboratories. It addresses benefits, risks, and ethical considerations, with emphasis on proportionality, privacy, and governance. Recommendations include approaches to sharing diverse genetic data types, establishing institutional policies, and addressing implementation barriers. This guidance aims to align Canadian clinical laboratory data-sharing practices with international standards and improve diagnostic accuracy, equity, and innovation in genomic medicine. By emphasizing ethical principles, proportionality, and governance, it seeks to enable responsible data sharing; strengthen trust among patients, families, and professionals; and contribute to the broader global genomic data ecosystem.

papers.title: Comparison of Next-Generation Sequencing and Quantitative PCR Methodologies for Quantification of Fungicide Resistance in Mixed Samples of Colletotrichum siamense .
papers.abstract: Measuring the frequency of fungicide resistance alleles in pathogen populations is critical for understanding resistance spread and severity. TaqMan quantitative PCR (qPCR) is a standard method for allele quantification, whereas next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies offer an alternative for high-resolution detection. Because studies exploring NGS for this purpose are limited, the objective of this study was to compare the accuracy and feasibility of Illumina NGS amplicon sequencing with that of a previously validated TaqMan qPCR assay to quantify resistance alleles to thiophanate-methyl fungicide in a set of mixed Colletotrichum siamense DNA samples. For validation, a set with known frequencies of resistance to thiophanate-methyl was used as a control. Both the NGS- and qPCR-based methods were highly precise, with an R 2 of 0.99 and 0.97, respectively, for the C. siamense DNA samples with known resistance frequencies. However, with the samples of unknown resistance frequencies that were collected from detached blueberry fruit assays, the NGS method demonstrated more variability than the TaqMan method ( P < 0.001). This variability was likely associated with low target DNA concentration and the presence of host and nontarget fungal DNA, which reduced PCR efficiency. This study highlighted strengths and weaknesses of both technologies and important assay design considerations. It was concluded that NGS-based methodologies may be preferential for large sample sizes and for detecting multiple or novel mutations within a region, whereas the qPCR assay can be more efficient for rapid quantification of known alleles.

papers.title: A 16-year retrospective investigation of granulomatous liver injury in immunocompetent and immunocompromised patients at a tertiary care center.
papers.abstract: Recent data on the underlying causes of granulomatous liver injury in the United States remain limited. In this study, we provide updated tertiary care center data on the causes of hepatic granulomas and evaluate the use of histochemical and molecular diagnostics to identify infectious organisms. We retrospectively reviewed 251 cases of hepatic granulomas (2009-2024) stratified by patient immune status. Additionally, we evaluated 6-year retrospective data from 2 institutions to determine the yield of broad-range molecular testing for infectious diseases. Causes of the 251 cases included idiopathic (31%), autoimmune disease (20%), steatohepatitis (19%), sarcoidosis (10%), infection (8%), and drug reaction (4%). A subset (9%) of idiopathic cases showed features highly suspicious for infection, but standard infectious stains were unrevealing, and none were initially sent for molecular testing. Retrospective evaluation of send-out pathogen molecular testing across both institutions revealed organism detection in 32% (12/37) and 50% (4/8) of highly suspicious cases, respectively. Increasing clinicopathologic suspicion correlated positively with successful molecular pathogen identification and inversely with false-positive contamination rates. Molecular testing is frequently underused by pathologists in the workup of granulomatous hepatitis. Pathologists should proactively leverage molecular diagnostics to optimize clinical decision-making when standard histochemical stains are unrevealing.

papers.title: Comprehensive mapping of essential-gene interactions in M. tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis, the causative agent of tuberculosis, remains the world's deadliest pathogen 1 . Despite intensive study, many of its genes remain uncharacterized, which limits the insight that can be gained into tuberculosis biology and constrains drug development. Genetic interaction (GI) mapping is a powerful strategy to define functional relationships between genes by quantifying how the phenotypic effects of combined perturbations deviate from expectations based on single-gene perturbations 2,3 . Here we develop a dual-sgRNA CRISPR-interference platform that enables high-throughput GI mapping in mycobacteria. We address key technical challenges in library construction and data interpretation by incorporating unique barcodes for each sgRNA pair and implementing a robust statistical pipeline for GI detection. Focusing on essential genes, we generate comprehensive GI maps in the model mycobacterium Mycobacterium smegmatis and the pathogen M. tuberculosis. These maps recapitulate known biology, uncover thousands of previously unrecognized interactions and identify functional connections between essential genes and drug targets. By generating AlphaFold3-based protein-protein interaction predictions 4 for all gene pairs in our GI maps, we show that a subset of GIs is likely to reflect underlying physical associations. Validation of selected GIs confirms both novel biological relationships and opportunities for synergistic targeting. Overall, this work establishes a generalizable framework for dual-gene perturbation and defines the architecture of essential-gene networks in mycobacteria, advancing both our understanding of tuberculosis biology and the rational design of combination therapies.

papers.title: Enteric infection and childhood stunting: strengthening causal inference from heterogeneous evidence.
papers.abstract: Laboratory detection of enteropathogens is associated with stunting in observational studies, but the pooled odds ratio does not estimate the effect of infection prevention or treatment on an individual child. Pathogen-domain and age-stratified estimates should not be read as equivalent causal effects; current data cannot reliably distinguish organisms, and environmental enteric dysfunction remains a hypothesized mediator, highlighting the need for prospective, longitudinal research to clarify causality. Prevention should integrate nutrition, infection control, and community-level environmental measures in the first 1000 days; empiric treatment of asymptomatic carriage is not supported, and prospective cohorts plus intervention trials are needed.

papers.title: The Participant Engagement and Cancer Genome Sequencing Network to accelerate research in rare and understudied cancers.
papers.abstract: The genomic characterization of cancers has considerably advanced research and clinical practice. However, critical gaps remain, including limited knowledge of tumor profiles in rare cancers and populations understudied in genomic research and insufficient integration of genomic, clinical and epidemiologic data. This Perspective highlights the Participant Engagement and Cancer Genome Sequencing (PE-CGS) Network, established by the US National Cancer Institute to address knowledge gaps in rare and understudied cancers. PE-CGS comprises five research centers supported by a coordinating center and guided by an external advisory panel. Collaborations across PE-CGS are grounded in shared values of participant-centeredness, engagement, access, collaboration and innovation. Activities emphasize participant engagement throughout the research process, including the return of results and collection of clinical and epidemiologic data alongside paired tumor/germline sequencing. PE-CGS demonstrates how engagement, return of results and comprehensive data collection can be integrated to support participant-centered cancer genomics research and accelerate research in rare and understudied cancers.
authors: Participant Engagement and Cancer Genome Sequencing (PE-CGS) Network

papers.title: Phenotypic and Genomic Characterization of Five Novel Klebsiella Bacteriophages: Exploring the Relationship Between Spot-Lysis Patterns and Host Defense Systems.
papers.abstract: Individual Klebsiella phages typically exhibit narrow host ranges; novel phages must therefore continue to be isolated and characterized to assemble phage therapy cocktails. However, the determinants governing host range remain unclear. To characterize five novel Klebsiella phages and examine relationships between their spot-lysis profiles and strain genotypes or host defense repertoires. Five sewage-derived phages were morphologically characterized, and their complete genomes were determined. Spot lysis was assessed against 249 clinical isolates of the Klebsiella pneumoniae species complex (KpSC). Genotypes, virulence and resistance determinants, and anti-phage defense systems were identified from draft genomes using Kleborate and DefenseFinder. Two phages were Myovirus-like and three Siphovirus-like, representing novel species within Jiaodavirus and Sugarlandvirus, and the known species Slopekvirus matisse. Overall, 160 of 249 isolates (64.3%) showed spot lysis with at least one phage; ΦKpT256 produced spot lysis in 137 isolates (55.0%), comparatively broad for a single phage. Spot lysis extended across diverse K/O loci, sequence types, and virulence/resistance profiles. Although 2,619 defense systems of 156 types were identified, descriptive comparison revealed no obvious one-to-one correspondence between spot-lysis patterns and individual defense systems. Spot-lysis patterns were not readily explained by the bacterial characteristics examined or by any single defense system, suggesting that additional host and phage factors may contribute. ΦKpT256 and the three Siphovirus-like phages showed differing species-level spot-lysis profiles and warrant evaluation as potential components of a KpSC-targeted phage cocktail.

papers.title: Spatial omics in cancer: a review of computational approaches and vision of AI-driven analysis.
papers.abstract: Predicting patient response to cancer treatments remains a challenge due to tumor heterogeneity and complex tumor microenvironments (TMEs). Modern spatial genomics technologies enable gene expression profiling alongside histological frameworks, but comprehensive analysis and clinical translation of these high-dimensionality datasets will benefit from Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML). This review synthesizes computational approaches that address challenges of spatial data by examining deep-learning architectures such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for histological feature extraction and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for modeling cell-cell interactions. We then explore the paradigm of Foundation Models that bridge histopathology with transcriptomics to accelerate the identification of spatially resolved biomarkers, improve patient stratification for immunotherapy and targeted treatments, and advance the clinical translation of mechanistic insights derived from the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Cancer-specific T cell receptor discovery using 150,000 clinical genomics samples.
papers.abstract: T cell receptors (TCRs) can enable detection and elimination of cancer cells via recognition of cancer-specific peptides presented on human leukocyte antigen (HLA). We speculated that shared cancer antigens could be recognized by recurrent ("public") TCRs, which might be identifiable using statistical methods. Here, we identified public TCRs against therapeutically relevant targets via computational analysis of large-scale bulk RNA sequencing data obtained from routine clinical genomics testing. Using data from ∼150,000 patient tumor samples, we identified TCR chains that were associated with well-known cancer antigens, including human papillomavirus, mutated KRAS, and CT83. We devised methods for pairing enriched TCR-α and TCR-β chain sequences and validated 44 TCRs across nine peptide-HLA targets for antigen recognition, including potent cytotoxic TCRs. Our results suggest that public anticancer TCRs are common and may represent a new source for the development of cancer therapeutics.

papers.title: Integrated Single-Step Duplex CRISPR-Based System for Point-of-Care Detection of Human Immunodeficiency Virus and Treponema pallidum Directly from Whole Blood.
papers.abstract: Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) and syphilis are two major sexually transmitted diseases that pose serious threats to public health, underscoring the urgent need for fast and sensitive diagnosis for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and Treponema pallidum (TP). Here, we developed a single-step duplex CRISPR assay that integrated reverse transcription, recombinase polymerase amplification, in vitro transcription, and CRISPR/Cas12a and Cas13a detection for simultaneous HIV and TP nucleic acid testing. We further engineered a fully integrated, low-cost microfluidic chip that consolidated whole-blood sample processing, nucleic acid release, and single-step duplex CRISPR detection. The chip featured a rapid plasma separator with a press-actuated design that removed inhibitors and extracted plasma within minutes without external equipment. The entire process was coupled with a homemade smartphone-based portable device that provided thermal incubation, dual-channel fluorescence excitation, and automated image analysis via a dedicated mobile application. This integrated system enables "sample-to-answer" detection within 30 min directly from whole blood, achieving a limit of detection of 2.5 copies/μL of both HIV and TP and demonstrating 100% sensitivity and specificity concordant with the real-time PCR in 51 cases of clinical samples. This work demonstrates a transformative point-of-care diagnostic platform that combines minimal user steps, equipment independence, and robust multiplex detection for decentralized pathogen testing.

papers.title: Gamma irradiation concerning genetics of Ralstonia solanacearum and export quality in potatoes.
papers.abstract: Potato brown rot, caused by Ralstonia solanacearum , is an important quarantine disease that can seriously affect tuber quality and limit the movement and marketability of potatoes. Gamma irradiation may help control the pathogen after harvest, but the dose used can also affect the nutritional value and quality of potato tubers. We aimed to study the genetic diversity of the potato brown rot pathogen, Ralstonia solanacearum, using molecular markers. We also evaluated how irradiation affects the physicochemical properties of treated and untreated potato tubers. Commercial potato varieties were collected from major potato-growing areas of Bangladesh for pathogen isolation and irradiation studies. Forty-two bacterial isolates were characterized on TTC medium and examined using PS-1/PS-2 PCR, 16S rRNA sequencing, phylotype-specific PCR, and mutS amplification. After irradiation, the tubers were assessed for weight loss, ascorbic acid, anthocyanin, carotenoid, total soluble solids (TSS), and mineral content. Virulent isolates produced the expected 553-bp PS-1/PS-2 amplicon. Sequence analysis placed a representative isolate close to Asian Ralstonia reference strains, while phylotype-specific PCR generated a 213-bp product corresponding to phylotype IV. The pathogen-specific 553-bp amplicon remained detectable up to 5.5 kGy but was not detected at 6 kGy under the conditions used in this study. A reduction in mutS band intensity was also observed following irradiation. The effects of irradiation on tuber quality varied with cultivar and dose. Ascorbic acid and carotenoid contents generally decreased with increasing irradiation dose, whereas anthocyanin and TSS remained comparatively stable. Mineral concentrations were generally higher in irradiated tubers than in untreated samples. Gamma irradiation reduced the detectability of the pathogen-specific PCR target, although this does not confirm complete pathogen inactivation. Irradiation conditions require optimization to balance pathogen suppression and nutritional quality. Further viability testing and genomic characterization are recommended.

papers.title: A single-cell atlas of pediatric undifferentiated recurrent fever reveals candidate immune regulators.
papers.abstract: Children with periodic fever syndromes not attributable to infections, rheumatic disorders, malignancies, or known monogenic autoinflammatory conditions are classified as "syndrome of undifferentiated recurrent fever" (SURF). To date, treatment remains empirical, often resulting in only a partial response, underscoring the unmet clinical need for new therapeutic strategies. To advance the molecular understanding of SURF, we generated a large-scale single-cell RNA-seq immune atlas of 29 SURF patients with more than 200,000 cells. Comparison of patients with three healthy cohorts revealed large-scale metabolic shifts together with a distinct cytokine signature already observable during afebrile periods. This indicates that afebrile SURF cannot be considered a less inflammatory resting state but rather as a distinct homeostatic state. Furthermore, our analysis suggests an NAMPT-mediated autocrine feedback loop connecting the metabolic dysregulations with the pro-inflammatory phenotype in monocytes. This study offers insights into the SURF immunopathology and generates testable hypotheses to guide future therapies.

papers.title: Understanding the impact of co-occurring diseases on aerial hyperspectral detection: A UAS case study with grapevine leafroll virus and downy mildew.
papers.abstract: Grapevine disease prevention and management challenges sustainable viticulture globally. Comprehensive vineyard monitoring is time- and labor-intensive, especially in regions where multiple pathogens regularly cause co-occurring infections. We used a visible-to-near-infrared (VNIR) imaging spectrometer mounted on an uncrewed aerial system (UAS) to monitor two New York State vineyards affected by grapevine downy mildew (GDM) and Grapevine Leafroll-associated Virus 3 (GLRaV-3). Four UAS datasets were collected during the 2024 growing season, accompanied by ground scouting, physiological measurements, and PCR diagnostics for a subset of vines. Partial least squares regression (PLSR) models detected GLRaV-3 symptoms with symptomatic-class F1 scores of 0.69-0.72 in August, and models differentiating GDM-only from GLRaV-3-only symptoms achieved accuracies of 0.55-0.82 after down-sampling. To test whether co-occurring GDM impacted accurate GLRaV-3 detection, we compared PLSR recall for GLRaV-3-only vines with recall for vines showing both GLRaV-3 and GDM symptoms. Across three datasets, recall differences (co-occurring minus GLRaV-3-only) were +0.4, +9.0, and -4.6 percentage points and all 95% confidence intervals included zero, suggesting that co-occurring GDM did not consistently reduce GLRaV-3 symptom classification accuracy. This study provides a direct, field-based evaluation of aerial imaging spectroscopy to detect co-occurring grapevine diseases in commercial vineyards. Our results suggest that UAS VNIR data can be informative amidst the biological complexity of ongoing operational agricultural systems. Early-season disease monitoring remains challenging, and larger representative studies are needed to better quantify co-occurrence effects on disease identification via aerial imaging spectroscopy.

papers.title: Photoelectrochemical biosensor using CoPP to quench PTCA for the detection of mip gene fragment.
papers.abstract: Legionella pneumophila is a harmful Gram-negative aquatic pathogen that causes Legionnaires' disease, and sensitive detection of this bacterium is essential for epidemiological investigation. Herein, a photoelectrochemical (PEC) biosensor based on 3,4,9,10-perylenetetracarboxylic acid (PTCA) as the photoactive material and tetraphenylporphyrin cobalt (CoPP) as the signal quencher was constructed for the detection of the macrophage infectivity potentiator (mip) gene fragment from Legionella pneumophila. PTCA with favorable optoelectronic properties and film-forming capacity provided a strong initial photocurrent response. Gold nanoparticles (Au NPs) were electrodeposited on the electrode surface to immobilize DNA S1 through Au-S interactions. After target-induced DNA hybridization, CoPP was intercalated into the formed DNA duplex, which efficiently quenched the PEC signal of PTCA. Benefiting from the signal quenching effect of CoPP towards PTCA, the proposed biosensor achieved quantitative detection of the mip gene fragment in the range from 100 fmol/L to 1 µmol/L with a detection limit of 33.3 fmol/L. This work provides an analytical tool and shows promise for practical screening of the mip gene fragment of Legionella pneumophila in respiratory specimens with high bacterial loads.

papers.title: Unsupervised clustering identifies candidate metabolic profiles, including an acidotic profile detectable before calving, in periparturient dairy cows.
papers.abstract: The metabolic status of periparturient dairy cows is highly heterogeneous, making it difficult for traditional assessment methods based on a single biomarker to comprehensively reflect systemic metabolic dysregulation. This study aimed to apply unsupervised clustering to identify distinct metabolic phenotypes using integrated blood physiological indicators and to evaluate the prepartum identifiability of metabolically compromised profiles. Venous blood samples were collected from 316 healthy Holstein cows (from - 7 to + 7 days relative to calving) across seven commercial farms in China for blood gas and electrolyte analysis. After data cleaning and variable selection, six key indicators-pH, PCO₂, HCO₃⁻, glucose, potassium, and sodium-were standardized and subjected to K-means clustering. The optimal number of clusters was determined to be three, yielding the following phenotypes: (1) a "metabolically compromised" group characterized by acidosis (low pH), hypercapnia (elevated PCO₂), hypoglycemia, and electrolyte imbalance; (2) a "normoacidemic-hyperkalemic" group with normal acid-base status but persistently elevated potassium; and (3) a "metabolically homeostatic" group exhibiting alkalotic tendencies, higher sodium and glucose levels, and stable electrolyte balance. A substantial proportion of cows already belonged to the metabolically compromised phenotype before calving, and its prevalence peaked during the mid-postpartum period (+ 4 to + 7 d). In unadjusted analyses, cows in this cluster exhibited modestly elevated postpartum β-hydroxybutyrate concentrations (P = 0.001) and significantly reduced milk protein percentage (P < 0.001); however, the BHBA association was not significant after adjusting for farm of origin in a mixed-effects model (P = 0.622), whereas the milk protein association remained robust. These findings indicate that impaired metabolic adaptation in this cluster is more consistently reflected by reduced milk protein than by elevated BHBA. Based on cluster centroids and validated by exploratory ROC analysis, prepartum thresholds for identifying the metabolically compromised profile were proposed: venous pH < 7.25 (AUC = 0.928), PCO₂ > 58.75 mmHg (AUC = 0.956), and glucose < 27.5 mg/dL (AUC = 0.876). Potassium was not retained as a discriminatory threshold because its AUC was only 0.577. These thresholds are exploratory and require validation in independent cohorts. These findings demonstrate that periparturient dairy cows segregate into three distinct metabolic states, and that a metabolically compromised acidotic profile can be identified antepartum. This provides a foundation for early risk stratification; future intervention studies are needed to determine whether targeting this profile improves clinical outcomes.

papers.title: MXene-based biosensors for pathogen detection: materials synthesis, sensing mechanisms, and analytical applications.
papers.abstract: Rapid and accurate pathogen detection is essential for disease diagnosis, food safety, environmental monitoring, and public health surveillance. Conventional detection techniques, including culture-based assays, polymerase chain reaction (PCR), high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), and immunoassays, require lengthy analysis time, complex sample preparation, high costs, and sophisticated instrumentation. These challenges have accelerated the development of MXene-based biosensors as promising alternatives for rapid and sensitive pathogen detection. Owing to their exceptional electrical conductivity, large specific surface area, tunable surface chemistry, and excellent biocompatibility, MXenes have emerged as attractive two-dimensional nanomaterials for biosensing applications. This review summarizes recent advances in MXene-based biosensors for pathogen detection, covering synthesis strategies, physicochemical properties, recognition elements, signal transduction mechanisms, and practical applications. Both top-down and bottom-up synthesis approaches are discussed to highlight their influence on MXene properties. The roles of antibodies, aptamers, nucleic acids, peptides, and molecularly imprinted polymers are critically examined, together with electrochemical, optical, fluorescence, and electrochemiluminescence sensing strategies. Furthermore, applications in food safety, environmental monitoring, clinical diagnostics, and wearable sensing devices are reviewed. Despite remarkable progress, challenges related to oxidation stability, restacking, poor long-term storage, batch-to-batch reproducibility, and scalable synthesis remain. These represent significant disadvantages of MXenes compared with conventional nanomaterials. Finally, future perspectives focus on green synthesis, multifunctional nanocomposites, wearable biosensors, and artificial intelligence-assisted data analysis. This review provides a comprehensive perspective on MXene-based biosensors and their potential for next-generation pathogen detection technologies.

papers.title: Cyperus scariosus- mediated synthesis of nickel-based nanomaterials for photocatalytic methylene blue degradation, antibacterial and antioxidant activities.
papers.abstract: The root extract of Cyperus scariosus (C. scariosus) was prepared in water and it was used for the synthesis of a nanomaterial based on nickel. The synthesized nanomaterial was tested for its photocatalytic, antibacterial and antioxidant properties. The maximum absorption wavelength obtained by the UV-visible analysis was ∼292 nm, with an apparent optical transition of ∼3.6 eV. The presence of crystalline features containing nickel and oxygen was confirmed by XRD, FTIR and EDX; however, unambiguous assignment of the reflection at 2θ = 32.58° was not possible and no phase purity was claimed. The image resolved features by SEM ranged from ca. 5-60 nm with a fitted distribution center of 33.5 ± 0.4 nm while the average hydrodynamic diameter by DLS was ca. 45 nm. The electrostatic colloidal stabilization was found to be limited with a zeta potential of around -14 mV. The material under sunlight irradiation resulted in about 96% of absorption reduction of methylene-blue in 50 min. The pseudo-first order rate constant was found to be 0.0153 min-1 at 298 K and 0.0286 min-1 at 343 K with an apparent activation energy of 12.04 kJ mol-1. After 5 reuses around 80% of degradation activity was maintained. An anti-bacterial and anti-oxidant response was also seen, and scavenger experiments indicated that more than one reactive species was involved, but did not identify a specific pathway. The results indicate that plant-based nickel-based materials could be used to treat dye-contaminated water, and suggest that more research is needed in this area. In the future, the mineralization, nickel release, ecotoxicity and performance of the system should be assessed in actual wastewater.

papers.title: Culture-negative peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis rates are decreased with water lysis but not 16S rRNA gene sequencing.
papers.abstract: ObjectivesA successful peritoneal dialysis (PD) programme should aim to have low peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis (PDAP) rates. Identification of the microbial organism enables targeted antibiotic treatment and allows for a root cause analysis to be performed. Culture-negative (CN) peritonitis presents a more challenging scenario whereby empirical treatment for Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms is commenced for 14 days, with Gram-negative cover discontinued based upon clinical response. In accordance with ISPD recommendations, we conducted a clinical quality improvement project in 2018 to decrease our culture-negative PDAP.MethodsFrom 2018 to 2021, our department had 336 cases of PDAP. The introduction of a water-lysis step and the application of 16S rRNA gene sequencing were implemented to reduce culture-negative PDAP.ResultsThere were 336 cases of PDAP between 2018 and 2021. In total, 135 cases occurred prior to the initiation of the water lysis step and 201 cases occurred after the introduction of the water lysis step and 16S rRNA sequencing. The rate of culture-negative PDAP prior to our change in PD effluent culture methodology was 33% (45/135); following changes to include a water lysis step and an increase in sample volume, the rate of culture-negative PDAP significantly fell to 20% (41/201) ( p < 0.01). 16S rRNA, using Sanger sequencing of culture-negative samples, did not significantly increase pathogen detection. Five out of 6 samples remained CN in the pre-water lysis step group, and 17 out of 23 samples also remained CN in the post-water lysis group ( p = 0.61).ConclusionsIntroduction of water lysis of peritoneal effluent significantly decreased culture-negative peritonitis rates, thus increasing organism identification and allowing for targeted antimicrobial therapy.

papers.title: Comparative and Sex-Specific Assessment of Proteomics, Clinical, and Genomic Data on Visceral Adipose Tissue Volume Using Machine Learning in UK Biobank: Advancing Precision Medicine.
papers.abstract: Visceral adiposity is a key driver of insulin resistance, which in turn is a strong risk factor for type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular diseases. We investigated the overall and sex-specific associations between plasma proteomics and visceral adipose tissue volume, and their intersection with clinical and genomic data to identify critical candidate proteins for visceral adiposity possibly linked to insulin resistance. We analyzed data from UK Biobank participants, using multistep machine learning to establish linear and nonlinear associations. The combined model, integrating clinical, proteomic, and polygenic data, accounted for 67% of visceral adipose tissue variance. Our research revealed significant protein interactions with environmental factors and identified sex-specific proteins correlated with visceral adipose tissue variance in both males and females. The findings suggest that a small number of plasma proteins explain a significant portion of the variance of visceral adipose tissue beyond nonproteomic measures, offering a potential single-source, personalized measurement of visceral adiposity that is easily accessible and may facilitate improved prediction and understanding of the biology of insulin resistance.

papers.title: Pathogen-specific positron emission tomography for Enterobacterales bone infection.
papers.abstract: Gram-negative bone infections involving Enterobacterales group of bacteria pose a growing concern, especially for orthopaedic surgeries and diabetic ulcers. Current imaging methods either identify morphological changes by CT and MRI, or inflammation, using white blood cell scans or 2-deoxy-2-[ 18 F]fluoro-d-glucose ([ 18 F]-FDG) positron emission tomography (PET). While valuable, these are not specific, resulting in delayed diagnoses. PET/CT using 2-deoxy-2-[ 18 F]fluoro-d-sorbitol ([ 18 F]-FDS) is a novel method for detecting living Enterobacterales bacteria in vivo, via a conserved sorbitol-specific bacterial pathway. In this study, we aim to evaluate [ 18 F]-FDS PET/CT for detection and monitoring of Enterobacterales bone infection in a mouse model. We adapted a murine model of Gram-positive implant-associated spine infection to a Gram-negative infection model. We compared microbiological techniques to imaging with [ 18 F]-FDG and [ 18 F]-FDS. We determined the standardized uptake value (SUV) ratios for detection of bacterial infection and response to therapy, in 48 mice with surgical implants infected with either Escherichia coli or Staphylococcus aureus and compared them to controls with surgical implants but no infection. Both bacteria induced substantial bone pathology with reduced bone density. [ 18 F]-FDS PET could specifically detect implant-associated spinal infections due to E. coli with a mean SUV ratio of 2.2 (SD 1.3), which was substantially lower in S. aureus (0.7 (SD 0.2); p = 0.002) and uninfected mice (1.0 (SD 0.1)). In contrast, [ 18 F]-FDG could not differentiate between the two bacterial infections or the control (p = 0.497). Finally, [ 18 F]-FDS PET could determine antibiotic efficacy, and monitor infection over time. We demonstrate that [ 18 F]-FDS affords a highly accurate and clinically translatable detection of Enterobacterales bone infection. This novel modality offers a rapid and specific method to diagnose and monitor bone infections, inform medical decisions, reduce the need for surgery, and limit unnecessary antibiotic use. Similar approaches may be implemented to develop tracers for other bacteria.

papers.title: The two-component system CrdRS mediates sub-inhibitory antibiotic-induced biofilm formation in Helicobacter pylori via bidirectional regulation of transporters PlpA and GlnP.
papers.abstract: Biofilm formation by Helicobacter pylori is a major driver of antibiotic tolerance and treatment failure, yet the signaling pathways that trigger biofilm development under sub-inhibitory antibiotic pressure remain poorly understood. Here, we show that sub-MIC levels of metronidazole, amoxicillin, and ciprofloxacin potently induce dense H. pylori biofilms. Through transcriptomic and genetic analyses, we identify the two-component system CrdRS as a central signaling hub that orchestrates this response via the bidirectional regulation of two ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters. Phosphorylated CrdR binds to AC-rich promoter motifs to directly activate plpA , which encodes a substrate-binding protein that drives exopolysaccharide secretion and matrix assembly. Concomitantly, CrdR represses glnP , which encodes an inner-membrane permease, thereby relieving transcriptional inhibition of the L-asparaginase gene ansB . This derepression triggers aberrant reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, which promotes oxidative stress-dependent biofilm maturation. Through phenotypic analysis of c rdRS deletion mutants, phosphorylation-defective point mutants (CrdR D53A and CrdS H173A ), and exogenous hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) induction, we demonstrate that CrdRS is required for mediating antibiotic-induced stress responses in a manner genetically separable from ROS sensing. Collectively, our findings establish a dual-mechanism model in which CrdRS orchestrates antibiotic-induced biofilm formation by simultaneously controlling matrix production and intracellular ROS generation. Notably, glnP expression was significantly lower in clinical multidrug-resistant isolates than in drug-sensitive ones, whereas plpA showed the opposite trend. These findings provide a mechanistic foundation for developing CrdRS-targeted strategies to combat biofilm-associated H. pylori infections.

papers.title: Age-dependent genetic effects contribute to immunosenescence in Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.abstract: Immunosenescence, the age-related decline in immune function, varies widely among individuals. Although both genetic and environmental factors contribute to variation in immunosenescence, the extent to which age-specific genetic effects shape age-related immune decline remains poorly understood. Here, we tested whether age-related variation in bacterial clearance is shaped by age-dependent genetic effects by measuring clearance of Escherichia coli infection in 175 genotypes at 1 wk of age and 183 genotypes at 5 wk of age. Clearance ability declined with age, but the magnitude of decline differed markedly among genotypes. Age-specific genetic effects explained substantially more phenotypic variation than age-independent genetic differences, and the genetic correlation in clearance ability across ages was modest, indicating that genetic effects on immune performance were only partially shared across ages. Consistent with these findings, genome-wide analyses identified largely distinct sets of candidate genes associated with clearance in young and old flies, including genes exhibiting genotype-by-age effects. Network and gene ontology analyses revealed enrichment for plasma membrane-associated genes and pathways involved in cell adhesion and cell migration. Functional follow-up of 14 candidate genes using hemocyte-specific RNA interference produced limited effects overall but confirmed that nebulosa contributes to bacterial clearance. Together, our results demonstrate that immunosenescence is shaped by age-dependent genetic effects and identify conserved pathways and candidate genes for future mechanistic studies of age-related immune decline.

papers.title: Quantitative Resistance to Aphanomyces Root Rot in Legumes.
papers.abstract: Aphanomyces root rot, caused by the soilborne oomycete Aphanomyces euteiches Drechs., is an important threat to legume crop production. In susceptible grain legumes, such as pea ( Pisum sativum ) and lentil ( Lens culinaris ), the disease can cause total yield loss under favorable infection conditions. No effective and durable method of disease control is currently available. Therefore, farmers are advised to prevent the spread of the pathogen through crop rotations with nonhost or resistant crops, and by monitoring soil inoculum levels using detection tests. Genetic resistance is an essential method for managing crop diseases. Indeed, significant progress has been achieved over the past three decades in identifying quantitative trait loci (QTL) for resistance to A. euteiches mainly in pea, but also in lentil, faba bean ( Vicia faba ), and the model species Medicago truncatula . These advances in genetics research have led to the recent registration in France of the first partially resistant pea varieties. This feature article provides a review of the research knowledge on the A. euteiches × legumes pathosystem, as well as plant sources of resistance, genetic determinants, and molecular mechanisms of quantitative resistance to A. euteiches currently being deciphered in pulse grains and the model legume species studied. It also highlights future research directions for the development of effective and durable resistance in legume varieties.

papers.title: Shotgun metagenomic characterization of human adenovirus F40 and a non-cpe Clostridium perfringens strain in pediatric prolonged diarrhea: a genome-resolved case study.
papers.abstract: Viral and bacterial pathogens may be concurrently detected in pediatric gastroenteritis, yet such findings are often missed by routine diagnostic methods. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing enables comprehensive detection and genomic characterization of microorganisms present in clinical specimens, including pathogens that may not be recovered by conventional testing. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed on a single pediatric diarrheic stool sample, followed by quality filtering, de novo assembly, taxonomic classification, phylogenetic reconstruction, and integrated virulome-resistome profiling, including plasmid-associated resistance elements. Routine diagnostics identified adenovirus as the sole pathogen. Metagenomic analysis confirmed human adenovirus F40 (HAdV-F40), showing close phylogenetic relatedness to globally distributed HAdV-F40 reference strains and a clear distinction from HAdV-F41. In addition, metagenomics uniquely detected a Clostridium perfringens strain (SAM_A8, ST-5) that was not recovered by culture. The strain lacked the classical enterotoxin gene (cpe) but harbored a conserved histotoxic virulence profile, including cpa, pfoA, colA, hyaluronidases, and sialidases. Plasmid-associated tetracycline resistance genes (tetA(P) and tetB(P)) were also identified. This case study demonstrates the feasibility of shotgun metagenomic sequencing for comprehensive detection and genomic characterization of microorganisms present in pediatric diarrheal stool specimens, including organisms not identified by routine diagnostics. The findings are descriptive and highlight the value of metagenomics as a complementary diagnostic approach. However, no conclusions regarding pathogenic synergy, causality, or the clinical contribution of the co-detected organisms can be drawn from this single case.

papers.title: A sequence-informed hybrid framework for predicting antibiotic minimum inhibitory concentrations in previously unseen Escherichia coli pathogens.
papers.abstract: When an Escherichia coli pathogen is newly encountered, antimicrobial susceptibility information may be incomplete or unavailable. We investigated whether minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) could be predicted for previously unseen pathogens by jointly using pathogen genomic sequence information, antibiotic characteristics, and observed pathogen-antibiotic MIC patterns. The predictive value of integrating pathogen genomic information, antibiotic characteristics, and observed pathogen-antibiotic MIC patterns within a hybrid collaborative-filtering framework for previously unseen E. coli pathogens remains unclear. To develop and evaluate Model C for predicting MIC values in previously unseen, genomically characterised E. coli pathogens. The study used 9377 E. coli pathogens, 26 antibiotics, and 51,554 exact MIC measurements among 243,802 possible pathogen-antibiotic combinations. Model C combined observed MIC patterns, genomic features related to antimicrobial resistance (AMR), nucleotide-sequence comparisons across 265 AMR-related loci, and antibiotic characteristics. Five-fold pathogen-out validation excluded all MIC measurements from each test pathogen from training and model selection. The common validation cohort contained 9058 pathogens and 50,460 observed MIC values; Models 3B and 3 were evaluated as comparators. In pathogen-out validation of the 50,460 observed MIC values, Model C achieved a mean absolute error of 0.5931 log₂ MIC units, root mean squared error of 0.8477, and Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.9055. Model C performed best overall. A final model fitted to all 50,460 observed MICs predicted the remaining 185,048 unmeasured MICs. Model C estimated MIC values for previously unseen E. coli pathogens using genomic, antibiotic, and observed interaction information. Independent external validation is required. Predictions may help prioritise confirmatory testing but should not replace antimicrobial susceptibility testing or be used alone to guide treatment.

papers.title: Mechanism Investigation of Platycodon grandiflorum Active Ingredients in Regulating Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition and Airway Remodeling in Asthma via Modulation of the Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A Axis and IL-17A/MAPK Pathway.
papers.abstract: Platycodon grandiflorum (Jacq.) A.DC. is a traditional Chinese medicinal herb recognized for its dual role as both food and medicine, renowned for its effects of diffusing the lung, alleviating sore throat, promoting expectoration, and facilitating pus drainage. In traditional medicinal practice, it is often used in combination with herbs such as Ephedra sinica , Prunus armeniaca and Glycyrrhiza uralensis utilized to mitigate symptoms associated with asthma, bronchitis, and other respiratory diseases. However, the therapeutic effects and molecular mechanisms of its principal bioactive components in treating asthma remain insufficiently characterized. To investigate the pharmacological effects and elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which triterpenoid saponins derived from Platycodon grandiflorum (PL-TS) inhibit airway epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and attenuate airway remodeling in asthma. Initially, the chemical constituents of the triterpenoid saponin fraction extracted from Platycodon grandiflorum (Jacq.) A. DC. (PL-TS) were identified by Ultra Performance Liquid Chromatography Tandem Mass Spectrometry (UPLC-MS). Subsequently, network pharmacology approaches were employed to predict potential therapeutic targets and core signaling pathways of PL-TS in asthma. An OVA-induced asthmatic mouse model was established for in vivo experiments. Airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR) was assessed via whole-body plethysmography (WBP), and histopathological changes in lung tissues were examined via hematoxylin-eosin (HE), Masson's trichrome, and periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) staining. Human bronchial epithelial cells (BEAS-2B) were utilized to establish an IL-17A-induced epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) model in vitro. Finally, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), immunohistochemistry (IHC), quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), and Western blotting (WB) were employed to investigate the modulatory effects of PL-TS on proteins associated with airway remodeling, the IL-17A/MAPK signaling pathway, and the Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A axis in both asthmatic mice and cellular models. UPLC-MS/MS analysis identified 38 triterpenoid saponins from PL-TS, providing a chemical foundation for subsequent mechanistic studies. Network pharmacology analysis revealed that the principal targets of PL-TS were predominantly enriched within the IL-17A signaling pathway. In OVA-induced asthmatic mice, PL-TS significantly attenuated inflammatory cell infiltration, mucus hypersecretion, and collagen deposition in lung tissues, while markedly reducing serum levels of IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, and OVA-IgE in vivo.
