Furthermore, PL-TS was found to inhibit the activation of the IL-17A/MAPK and Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A signaling pathways in both mouse lung tissue and stimulated cells, while downregulating EMT-related protein Vimentin, Snail, and N-cadherin, upregulating expression of E-cadherin. suppressing the phosphorylation of p38, ERK, and JNK in the MAPK pathway. In addition, PL-TS downregulated Sirt6 expression and reduced RORγt and IL-17A levels, suggesting a potential involvement of the Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A regulatory axis, although the precise epigenetic mechanism requires further investigation. This study demonstrated that the PL-TS significantly alleviated airway inflammation, mucus hypersecretion, and airway remodeling in asthma model. The effects were associated with suppression of the IL-17A/MAPK pathway and downregulation of the Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A axis, suggesting a potential dual mechanism that highlight its therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Conversational Multi-Agentic Network-Driven Disease Module Identification and Drug Repurposing Prediction With ChatDRex: Platform Development Study.
papers.abstract: Repurposing approved drugs offers a time- and cost-effective alternative to traditional drug development. However, in silico prediction of repurposing candidates is challenging and requires the effective collaboration of specialists in various fields, including pharmacology, medicine, biology, and bioinformatics. Fragmented, specialized algorithms and tools often address only narrow aspects of the overall problem. Heterogeneous, unstructured data landscapes require the expertise of specialized users. Hence, diverse data sources might not integrate smoothly across workflows. We aimed to develop an integrated, natural language-driven system that enables domain experts to conduct complex network-based drug repurposing analyses by integrating heterogeneous biomedical data sources and specialized bioinformatics methods within a unified workflow. With ChatDRex, we present a conversation-based, multi-agent system that facilitates the execution of complex bioinformatic analyses aiming for network-based drug repurposing prediction. It builds on the integrated systems medicine knowledge graph NeDRexDB. ChatDRex provides natural language access to its extensive biomedical knowledge base. It integrates bioinformatics agents for network analysis, literature mining, and drug repurposing. These are complemented by agents that evaluate functional coherence for in silico validation. Its flexible multi-agent design assigns specific tasks to specialized agents, including query routing, data retrieval, algorithm execution, and result visualization. A dedicated reasoning module keeps the user in the loop and allows for hallucination detection. ChatDRex operationalizes complex network-based drug repurposing workflows through conversational interaction, integrating biomedical knowledge access with algorithm execution and validation-oriented assessments. Its modular multi-agent architecture enables scalable task specialization across retrieval, analysis, validation, and visualization, while the reasoning module provides transparency and safeguards against unreliable outputs. By enabling researchers with limited computational expertise to control complex analyses with natural language, ChatDRex could democratize access to bioinformatics as an important resource for drug repurposing. It could enable clinical experts to generate hypotheses and explore drug repurposing opportunities, ultimately accelerating the discovery of novel therapies and advancing personalized medicine and translational research.

papers.title: Multi-virus Wastewater Surveillance in Heterogeneous Urban-Sewage Systems: Comparative Insights From Sewage Treatment Plants and Open Drains.
papers.abstract: Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has been applied for public health surveillance for several decades but gained unprecedented global prominence during the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to its broader adoption for multi-pathogen surveillance. However, the impact of heterogeneous urban wastewater infrastructure on the detection and interpretation of pathogen signals remains inadequately characterised, particularly in settings such as Mumbai, with fragmented and partially connected sewer networks. This study systematically compared multi-pathogen wastewater surveillance from centralised sewage treatment plants (STPs) and decentralised open drains (ODs), which represent aggregated and localised population catchments, respectively. Wastewater was collected during two monitoring periods (2023 and 2024) and analysed by RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2, influenza viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Comparative analyses included detection frequency, temporal dynamics, and patterns of viral co-occurrence between node types. Viral detection rates were highest in STP influent, consistent with signal integration over larger populations and reduced short-term variability. Conversely, open drains exhibited greater temporal fluctuation, which may be consistent with localised, short-term changes but with reduced signal persistence. In the absence of concurrent clinical data, these node-level differences are interpreted as patterns in the wastewater signal rather than demonstrated gains in epidemiological sensitivity or earlier detection. SARS-CoV-2 was consistently detected across both node types, while influenza virus detection was more sporadic and exhibited marked variability, suggesting seasonal transmission dynamics. Co-detection of influenza A and B was observed in 2023, and influenza A subtyping revealed limited within-type diversity; source attribution for the detected subtypes could not be determined. Collectively, these findings indicate that wastewater signal profiles reflect an interplay between pathogen-specific characteristics and the structural configuration of the sampling network. Overall, the findings support integrated surveillance frameworks that leverage both centralised and decentralised nodes, while highlighting the need for extended temporal monitoring and independent clinical validation to strengthen epidemiological inference.

papers.title: Genomic rearrangement of the capsule operon in a phylogenetically distinct cluster of the multi-drug-resistant Escherichia coli lineage ST131.
papers.abstract: Escherichia coli ST131 is a dominant cause of multi-drug-resistant extraintestinal infections in humans. The lineage has a three-clade phylogenetic structure, of which clade C has gained resistance to multiple classes of antibiotics and is globally disseminated. As well as antimicrobial resistance, a number of virulence factors contribute to the success of ST131 clade C, including the production of capsule. Previous work on a limited number of strains has shown that the capsule operon in ST131 is highly variable. In this study, we analyzed the capsule genetics of E. coli ST131 by interrogating 3,033 genomes. Our data show a clonal distribution of capsule types and identify a monophyletic group of ST131 clade C strains that are characterized by an atypical capsule operon with highly divergent alleles of the key kpsM and kpsT genes. Our analysis suggests there is ongoing evolution within clade C of ST131, which looks to be driven not by the continuing evolution of antimicrobial resistance but by host-pathogen interactions.IMPORTANCEMulti-drug-resistant (MDR) Escherichia coli is a problematic cause of invasive disease in humans and animals. Resistance to multiple classes of antibiotics is severely limiting treatment options. ST131-C is a highly successful, MDR clone of E. coli that is a major cause of extraintestinal infections. Capsule is a key virulence factor in contributing to this clone's success, with capsule switching allowing the bacteria flexibility to thrive in different niches. We present evidence that suggests continual evolution of this proliferant clone influenced by host-pathogen interaction. Small genetic changes can define the success of a clone; therefore, it is important to monitor this continual evolution in pathogens.

papers.title: Enterobacteriaceae and Bacteriophages: Implications Against Antimicrobial Resistance.
papers.abstract: Enterobacteriaceae represent a clinically challenging bacterial family owing to the global emergence of multidrug resistance. Bacteriophages, the natural predators of these bacteria, have emerged as powerful tools for detecting, targeting, and inhibiting these pathogens. This review provides a comprehensive overview of bacteriophages targeting Enterobacteriaceae hosts, focusing on their diversity, virion architecture, and the molecular determinants of host specificity. The dynamic co-evolution between bacterial defence strategies and phage counter-defences is discussed to illustrate the complexity of the phage-Enterobacteriaceae host interactions. Translational applications of Enterobacteriaceae phages, including phage therapy, engineered phages, phage-derived lysins as antimicrobials, and phage-based diagnostics for rapid and specific pathogen detection is also explored alongside their limitations including limited large-scale clinical trials, regulatory and manufacturing hurdles, and the need for robust host-range prediction and standardization. Overall, this review elaborates implications of bacteriophage-Enterobacteriaceae interactions to combat antimicrobial resistance and support the development of next-generation antibacterial therapies and diagnostics.

papers.title: The LbBLH9-LbGeBP module regulates salt gland development and salt tolerance in Limonium bicolor.
papers.abstract: GLABROUS1 enhancer-binding protein (GeBP) transcription factors play pivotal roles in the regulating plant development and stress responses. However, the function of GeBP family members in regulating salt gland development and salt tolerance in Limonium bicolor remains unclear. In this study, the gene LbGeBP1 exhibited high expression levels during the early stages of salt gland development. We found that LbGeBP1 is mainly expressed in salt glands and LbGeBP1 localizes in the nucleus. Functional analysis through overexpression and knockout of LbGeBP1 in L. bicolor showed that LbGeBP1 negatively regulates salt gland development and salt tolerance. Further investigation revealed that the BEL1-like homeobox (BLH) LbBLH9 binds to the LbGeBP1 promoter and represses its expression. LbBLH9 was specifically expressed in salt glands. In contrast to LbGeBP1, LbBLH9 was found to positively regulate salt gland development and salt tolerance. Consistent with this regulatory relationship, silencing LbBLH9 in the LbGeBP1-overexpression background further increased LbGeBP1 expression and exacerbated defects in salt gland development and salt secretion. In contrast, simultaneous silencing of LbBLH9 and LbGeBP1 partially rescued the defects caused by silencing LbBLH9 alone. Together, these molecular and genetic data support a model in which LbBLH9 promotes salt gland development and salt tolerance by repressing the transcription of LbGeBP1. Furthermore, the LbBLH9-LbGeBP1 module regulates the expression of genes involved in salt gland development and salt stress responses. This study reveals a novel molecular mechanism governing salt gland development and salt tolerance in L. bicolor, providing a theoretical foundation for elucidating salt tolerance mechanisms in plants.

papers.title: Investigating the Distinctive Clinical and Genetic Landscape of PPA2 Deficiency.
papers.abstract: PPA2 encodes for inorganic pyrophosphatase 2, a mitochondrial enzyme that hydrolyzes inorganic pyrophosphates into orthophosphate. Biallelic loss-of-function variants cause PPA2 deficiency, an emerging recessive cardiac condition that causes heart failure and sudden cardiac death in infants and young people. Using published case reports and large-scale genomics resources, we defined the clinical and molecular spectrum of this disease, classified variants using a customized American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics pipeline, assessed genotype-phenotype correlations, calculated predicted prevalence using the gnomAD GenIE tool, and investigated monoallelic associations in the UK Biobank. A total of 63 cases from 37 families were identified from 12 publications. The natural history of this disease is characterized by clinical heterogeneity and high mortality (79% by 20 years of age), typically presenting as a highly arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy with 2 distinct risk periods: in infancy, where viral infections can lead to heart failure, and in adolescence, where minimal alcohol exposure can trigger sudden cardiac death. The disease is genetically heterogeneous, with 29 distinct variants described (18 of which were classified as [likely] pathogenic), usually in compound heterozygosity. As complete gene knockout appears to be incompatible with life, PPA2 deficiency is caused by biallelic variants within a particular loss-of-function window, with deficiency mitigated by hypomorphic effects, variants in nonconstitutive exons, and particular compound heterozygous combinations. The spectrum of phenotypic effect extends to monoallelic carriers of pathogenic variants, which demonstrate an apparent mitohormesis-like compensatory protection from heart failure. The disease has an estimated prevalence of at least 1/135 000 in European ancestry populations. PPA2 deficiency is a genetically complex and clinically severe disease. Given the potential for effective life-saving interventions, PPA2 may warrant inclusion in emerging newborn genomic screening programs.

papers.title: KARS1-Related Infantile-Onset Progressive Leukoencephalopathy With or Without Deafness: A Novel Variant and Phenotypic Expansion.
papers.abstract: Biallelic variants in the KARS1 gene, encoding lysyl-tRNA synthetase, are responsible for autosomal recessive disorders such as infantile-onset progressive leukoencephalopathy with or without deafness (LEPID; OMIM #619147) and nonsyndromic hearing loss (DFNB89). Common features of LEPID include sensorineural hearing loss, developmental delay, and leukoencephalopathy, but dysmorphic facial features and cardiac anomalies are not commonly reported. This study presents the first documented LEPID case in Iran, expanding the phenotypic and genetic spectrum of KARS1-related disorders. Whole exome sequencing (WES) was performed on a two-year-old Iranian boy from non-consanguineous parents, without a positive history of any neurologic conditions. Identified variants were validated by Sanger sequencing, with familial segregation analysis. Moreover, a literature review of 41 KARS1-related cases was conducted to compare clinical and genetic findings. WES identified two compound heterozygous KARS1 variants (NM_005548.3): c.959G > A (p.Arg320His) and c.2T > C (p.Met1Thr), previously reported and novel, respectively, both of which were classified as likely pathogenic according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics criteria. The patient exhibited typical LEPID features (sensorineural hearing loss, developmental delay, seizures, leukoencephalopathy) alongside unprecedented dysmorphic facial features (e.g., synophrys, pointed triangular chin) and cardiac anomalies (pulmonary stenosis, atrial septal defect). Literature review confirmed these dysmorphic features as novel, absent in prior cases, with cardiac involvement in a limited number of patients. This study highlights a novel KARS1 variant and an expanded phenotypic spectrum of LEPID, emphasizing the role of WES in diagnosing rare disorders even in non-consanguineous marriages. These findings advocate for broader phenotypic recognition and functional studies to elucidate KARS1's role in neurodevelopmental, craniofacial, and cardiac abnormalities.

papers.title: Protein large language model-assisted one-to-one gene homology mapping in cross-species single-cell transcriptome integration.
papers.abstract: Cross-species integration of single-cell transcriptomes requires establishing gene correspondences to enable comparative analysis of expression profiles across organisms. Current approaches predominantly rely on Ensembl homology tables; although gene-family expansion and contraction can reflect biologically meaningful evolutionary divergence, default many-to-many mappings can overweight expanded gene-family signals during integration and generate mapping-associated microclusters that lack clear cell-type identity, thereby complicating direct cell-type alignment. Although restricting mappings to a one-to-one scheme suppresses such artifacts, it reduces the number of homology gene pairs by ∼8% (about 900 pairs). To address this limitation, we develop a protein large language model (pLLM)-based gene homology mapping strategy that boosts the number of homology gene pairs. By enforcing a one-to-one mapping constraint and integrating pLLM-derived representations with sequence similarity, we construct a fused mapping approach, which achieves top performance in a comprehensive benchmark based on a curated cross-species atlas spanning nine data sets, 11 species, and more than 3.2 million cells. Our method further identifies previously unannotated cell-type marker pairs, facilitating novel cross-species marker discovery. These results establish a robust framework for gene homology mapping in cross-species transcriptome integration, improving both accuracy and biological interpretability.

papers.title: Genomic characterization of carbapenem-resistant organisms from pediatric patients with hematological malignancies and genomic comparison of infection versus intestinal colonizing strains.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to characterize the species distribution, sequence types, and antimicrobial resistance mechanisms of carbapenem-resistant organisms (CROs) in pediatric patients with hematological malignancies, and to clarify the genomic relationship between clinical infectious CROs and intestinal colonizing CROs. Non-duplicate infectious CRO strains and paired intestinal colonizing CROs were collected from 2020 to 2024. Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analyses were performed to identify bacterial species, multilocus sequence types, resistance genes, mobile genetic elements, and genomic relatedness. Seven CRO species were identified, dominated by Pseudomonas aeruginosa , Klebsiella pneumoniae , and Enterobacter hormaechei . A total of 34 carbapenem resistance-associated genes were detected, with efflux pump overexpression and antibiotic inactivation as the main mechanisms. Three patients carried both infectious and intestinal CROs. Two pairs showed nearly identical genomes (average nucleotide identity >99.99%), confirming infections originated from intestinal colonization. One pair belonged to different species but shared an identical KPC-2 gene located on the same Tn 7247 -like transposon, indicating potential horizontal gene transfer. Diverse CROs and corresponding resistance mechanisms are prevalent in pediatric patients with hematological malignancies. This study identifies the dominant CRO species and key resistance mechanisms in this high-risk population, supporting the gastrointestinal tract as a potential reservoir for CROs, and indicating the likelihood of horizontal transmission of carbapenemase genes. These findings underscore the necessity of intensive surveillance and strict infection control measures to curb the dissemination of CROs in vulnerable pediatric populations. Carbapenem-resistant organisms (CROs) cause life-threatening infections in pediatric patients with hematological malignancies, who are highly vulnerable due to chemotherapy-induced immunosuppression. This study characterized CRO species, resistance mechanisms, and genomic links between infectious and intestinal colonizing strains in this population. We confirmed that intestinal colonization is an important source of subsequent CRO infections and identified interspecies horizontal transfer of the carbapenemase gene KPC-2 via a Tn 7247 -like transposon. These findings highlight the critical need for enhanced intestinal CRO screening and strict infection control measures to protect this vulnerable pediatric group.

papers.title: Caspofungin-induced β-(1,3)-glucan unmasking is associated with enhanced innate immune clearance of Candida (Candidozyma) auris .
papers.abstract: Candida auris is an emerging multidrug-resistant fungal pathogen that avoids early host immune detection by masking immunostimulatory β-(1,3)-glucan beneath a dense outer mannan layer. Whether caspofungin-induced cell wall remodeling can increase β-(1,3)-glucan exposure and alter innate immune interactions in C. auris remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigate how sublethal concentrations of caspofungin induce cell wall remodeling and modulate innate immune responses. Sublethal caspofungin concentrations were used to maintain normal growth kinetics while allowing cell wall remodeling. Caspofungin treatment increased β-(1,3)-glucan surface exposure across Candida strains, with the strongest response observed in C. auris strain 1100. This increase was supported by fluorescence microscopy, Cy3-positive cell quantification, and ImageJ-based analysis of fluorescence intensity and stained surface area. Scanning electron microscopy showed surface changes consistent with caspofungin-treated cell wall remodeling. Caspofungin-treated Candida cells exhibited enhanced uptake by RAW 264.7 macrophages and increased macrophage-mediated clearance at early and intermediate time points. In C. auris , this increased clearance persisted over 24 h, whereas the effect diminished in C. albicans , consistent with species-specific differences in macrophage interaction and intracellular survival. Finally, in the Galleria mellonella infection model, larvae infected with caspofungin-pretreated cells showed improved survival and reduced fungal burden compared with larvae infected with untreated controls. Together, these findings show that sublethal caspofungin exposure is associated with increased β-(1,3)-glucan exposure, cell wall remodeling, and enhanced innate immune clearance of C. auris . These results support fungal cell wall remodeling as a potential adjunct strategy to improve host-mediated control of multidrug-resistant Candida infections.IMPORTANCE C. auris is a dangerous fungal pathogen that is difficult to treat and can evade the body's immune defenses. One reason for its success is its ability to hide key cell wall components that immune cells normally recognize. In this study, we show that low, non-lethal levels of the antifungal drug caspofungin can alter the fungal cell wall in a way that exposes these hidden immune signals. This exposure is associated with improved recognition, engulfment, and killing of C. auris by immune cells. Using imaging, immune cell assays, and an infection model, we show that caspofungin-induced cell wall remodeling is associated with enhanced immune clearance and reduced fungal burden. These findings reveal an additional benefit of echinocandin treatment and suggest that antifungal drugs may help the immune system fight infection, even at doses that do not directly kill the fungus.

papers.title: Bacterial etiology of acute otitis media with spontaneous otorrhea in Spanish children: molecular insights from a multicenter study.
papers.abstract: Acute otitis media (AOM) is one of the most prevalent infectious diseases in childhood, with Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae being the most commonly involved pathogens. Following the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic and the incorporation of 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV13) into the national immunization program, changes in pneumococcal invasive disease have been described, but data on AOM remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the current bacterial etiology of pediatric AOM. Spontaneous otorrhea fluid (SOF) samples and optional nasopharyngeal samples (NP) were collected from children with AOM attending 13 primary care centers in southern Barcelona. Conventional culture and PCR were used for pathogen detection. Most frequent pathogens ( Streptococcus pyogenes , S. pneumoniae , and H. influenzae ) underwent antimicrobial susceptibility testing and whole-genome sequencing. A total of 145 SOF and 83 NP samples were obtained. Bacterial growth in SOF samples was detected by culture in 80.7% of the samples and by molecular methods in 91.7%. The predominant pathogens were H. influenzae (40.7%), S. pyogenes (35.2%), and S. pneumoniae (33.8%). Serotype 3 (mainly GPSC12-CC180) was the most frequent pneumococcal serotype (15.6%), and 23.8% of identified serotypes were included in PCV13 despite high vaccination coverage. Most of the S. pyogenes analyzed (43.1%) belonged to the emm1 -ST28 genotype, and 94.1% of H. influenzae isolates analyzed were non-typeable. These findings demonstrate a marked shift in AOM etiology in the post-PCV13 era, with H. influenzae emerging as the leading pathogen and an increase in S. pyogenes AOM. Continued surveillance is essential to inform future vaccination and prevention strategies. This multicenter study provides new insights into the current epidemiology of acute otitis media (AOM) in children vaccinated with the 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine. First, it underscores the role of molecular methods in pathogen detection. Second, it adds new evidence of the lack of concordance between nasopharyngeal and spontaneous otorrhea fluid samples, particularly for S. pneumoniae . Third, whole-genome analysis confirmed the predominance of the GSPC12-clade Ia as the major contributor to the vaccine failures due to serotype 3 pneumococci. Fourth, we characterized the S. pyogenes lineages associated with its recent upsurge in AOM, which differs from those causing invasive disease in our area. Finally, our findings confirm the current dominance of non-typeable H. influenzae as the leading cause of AOM in vaccinated children.

papers.title: Bridging a genetic gap with new tools to study the metabolism, fitness, and virulence in Burkholderia cenocepacia .
papers.abstract: Burkholderia cenocepacia is a formidable opportunistic pathogen, particularly in individuals with cystic fibrosis, yet its study has long been hampered by limited availability of genetic tools due to its high intrinsic antibiotic resistance. A recent study by M. M. Noe, K. Meesilpavikkai, Y. Ajimathorn, A. Sawatpanich, et al. (Microbiol Spectr 14:e02492-25, 2026, https://doi.org/10.1128/spectrum.02492-25) addresses this bottleneck by adapting a unified trimethoprim-selectable toolkit for markerless gene deletion and site-specific chromosomal complementation. By applying these tools to the purM gene, the authors demonstrate that while purM is universally essential for de novo purine biosynthesis, its role in intracellular survival is strain-dependent. These findings highlight the metabolic heterogeneity within the Burkholderia cepacia complex and provide a robust methodological framework for future functional genomics to help elucidate the metabolism, fitness, and virulence of these important bacteria. This commentary discusses how these advancements simplify complex genetic workflows and open new avenues for investigating the metabolic determinants of Burkholderia pathogenesis and fitness.

papers.title: Wastewater-based genomic surveillance uncovers broader SARS-CoV-2 diversity and spatial transmission dynamics in Georgia, January 2023-July 2024.
papers.abstract: Wastewater surveillance of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) using next-generation sequencing (NGS) enables real-time monitoring of circulating and emerging variants, often providing earlier detection than clinical reporting while capturing presymptomatic, asymptomatic, and symptomatic infections. However, the correlation between lineage abundance in wastewater and clinical specimens from corresponding sewersheds in Georgia remains understudied. From January 2023 through July 2024, the Georgia Public Health Laboratory (GPHL) sequenced SARS-CoV-2 from 669 wastewater samples collected across 17 treatment facilities in 15 counties. These data were compared with 325 clinical specimens from corresponding sewersheds to assess early detection potential. Nucleic acids were extracted using the KingFisher Apex platform, followed by genomic library preparation and paired-end whole-genome sequencing on the Illumina NextSeq 2000. Variant calling and lineage abundance estimation using Freyja identified 2,218 SARS-CoV-2 lineages and sub-lineages, 1,769 in 2023, and 1,255 in 2024, with 806 co-circulating across both years. Clinical sequences spanned 135 lineages/sub-lineages across 15 clades, with >70% in clades 24A (27.4%), 23A (19.4%), 23F (13.5%), and 22E (10.2%). Predominant lineages included XBB.1.5 (11.4%), JN.1 (6.8%), and JN.1.4 (6.2%), reflecting broader clinical trends in Georgia. Clinical data also reflected distinct transmission patterns, including viral introduction and spread within and between counties. Overall, this study provides important insights into the introduction and dissemination of SARS-CoV-2 lineages in Georgia. Expanding wastewater surveillance to include other emerging and reemerging pathogens of public health importance will be particularly valuable during periods of low disease incidence, serving as an early warning system when clinical testing is limited and enabling timely public health responses.IMPORTANCEWastewater-based surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 provides a noninvasive, cost-effective, population-level method for detecting viral genetic material independent of clinical testing. Next-generation sequencing enables timely monitoring of circulating lineages by public health laboratories. The Georgia National Wastewater Surveillance System (GA-NWSS) established in 2021 through collaboration between the Georgia Department of Public Health (DPH) Epidemiology and the Georgia Public Health Laboratory (GPHL) collects weekly samples from 17 wastewater treatment facilities across 15 counties. From January 2023 through July 2024, GPHL sequenced 669 wastewater samples, identifying 2,218 SARS-CoV-2 lineages and sub-lineages, compared with 135 lineages detected in 325 clinical specimens from corresponding sewersheds. Spatial analysis highlights viral spread across state boundaries and within Georgia catchment areas, illustrating evolving transmission patterns. These results demonstrate that wastewater sequencing captures broader genomic diversity than clinical sampling alone, emphasizing its critical role in pathogen genomic surveillance and supporting data-driven public health response to SARS-CoV-2.

papers.title: An rRNA hybridization-based approach for rapid and accurate identification of diverse fungal pathogens.
papers.abstract: Invasive fungal infections are a global threat for which early diagnosis is critical for patient outcomes, but current diagnostic measures remain notoriously slow. Here, we extend our multiplexed, hybridization-based rRNA-targeted strategy for rapid, sensitive pathogen identification, previously designed for diverse bacteria and Candida species, to identify diverse fungal pathogens. We created a set of 91 probes targeting 86 medically relevant fungal species, designed to recognize regions of differential conservation across taxonomic groupings, from class- to species-specific probes. We assessed assay performance across a Training Set of 93 clinical isolates spanning 32 species of common fungal pathogens across 18 genera, with Pearson correlations of probeset reactivity profiles identifying the pathogen at the species, genus, and family level with 83%, 94%, and 95% accuracy, respectively, in a leave-one-out analysis. We developed a new classifier on this Training Set, using taxonomic categories to select progressively more informative probes at each taxonomic level. After optimization, we assessed performance on an independent Validation Set of 54 clinical isolates spanning the same species as the Training Set, with 91%, 94%, and 98% at the species, genus, and family levels, respectively. We piloted our assay on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue, demonstrating rapid, culture-independent fungal identification from this high-value clinical sample type, often the sole specimen available. The assay requires <30 min hands-on time (or <65 min from FFPE tissue), returning results in <8 h from cultured specimen on an RNA detection platform available in clinical laboratories.IMPORTANCETimely identification of fungal pathogens is critical for patient outcomes. Here we describe a multiplexed hybridization-based assay targeting rRNA that capitalizes on the high sequence conservation and abundance of rRNA to generate unique reactivity profiles that serve as "fingerprints" of diverse fungal pathogens. By comparing these fingerprints to a Training Set of known isolates, this novel assay enables accurate identification of 32 species of pathogenic fungi from crude lysates of cultured clinical isolates.

papers.title: A comparative study of mNGS and tNGS for pathogen detection in paired upper and lower respiratory tract specimens from pediatric pneumonia patients.
papers.abstract: High-throughput sequencing technologies have become essential tools in clinical diagnostics, but the comparative performance of targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) versus metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) in pediatric respiratory infections remains unclear. In this study, paired throat swab and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) specimens were collected from children with lower respiratory tract infections. Both tNGS and mNGS were used to detect pathogens in paired samples. For the same specimen type, tNGS and mNGS showed strong agreement, with Kappa coefficients of 0.791 ( P < 0.001) for BALF and 0.757 ( P < 0.001) for throat swabs. Although the pathogen profiles of the upper and lower respiratory tracts differed, when using the same detection method, the agreement between the two anatomical sites remained substantial, with Kappa values of 0.659 ( P < 0.001) for mNGS and 0.590 ( P < 0.001) for tNGS-both approaching or reaching the threshold for strong consistency. These findings confirm that tNGS is a reliable alternative to mNGS for pediatric respiratory pathogen detection, and that even between different respiratory sites, the diagnostic agreement is high enough to support clinical decision-making. This study demonstrates that, for the same specimen type, tNGS and mNGS achieve substantial agreement in detecting respiratory pathogens in children (Kappa 0.791 for BALF and 0.757 for throat swabs). Thus, tNGS offers a cost-effective alternative to mNGS for routine pediatric respiratory diagnostics. Importantly, despite distinct pathogen profiles between the upper respiratory tract (URT) and lower respiratory tract (LRT), substantial diagnostic concordance was observed between paired throat swab and BALF specimens tested with identical sequencing approaches (Kappa = 0.659 for mNGS, 0.590 for tNGS). This observation bears meaningful clinical relevance, suggesting that URT throat swabs could provide diagnostically helpful etiological clues. Still, BALF sampling retains critical value for identifying pathogens predominantly residing in the lower respiratory tract, and throat swab results require prudent clinical interpretation.

papers.title: Deciphering the modular structure of phage depolymerase: a dual-action strategy for biofilm degradation and targeted Pseudomonas aeruginosa binding.
papers.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a critical ESKAPE pathogen that can form strong biofilms, which protect it from antibiotics and the host's immune system. Enzymes from bacteriophages, called depolymerases, are often found in tail fiber proteins and provide a useful way to break down these biofilms. In this work, we studied ORF55, a tail fiber protein from Pseudomonas phage phiPA1-3 that contains an SGNH hydrolase domain. Using AlphaFold2 for structural modeling and modular dissection, we identified the specific functions of its N-terminal and C-terminal parts. We found that the full protein (SGNH55_Full) broke down easily. However, a shorter version that kept the SGNH hydrolase domain (SGNH55Δtail_619) was much more stable and better at degrading biofilms. This truncated enzyme worked well against biofilms from clinical isolates, including those resistant to phages. This shows it has broad potential for treatment that does not depend on the virus itself infecting the bacteria. At the same time, we identified the N-terminal domain (TFP55) as the part responsible for binding to the bacterial receptor. We used TFP55 to develop a fast latex agglutination test to detect P. aeruginosa . This test was very specific and sensitive, with a limit of detection of 10 CFU, and it stayed stable for 6 months. Our results show that breaking down phage tail fibers into modules is a powerful strategy. It provides a clear path for creating both effective anti-biofilm agents and stable tools for diagnosis.IMPORTANCEBiofilm-forming Pseudomonas aeruginosa poses severe clinical challenges, and full-length phage depolymerases, while promising, are often unstable. This study overcomes this limitation through the structure-guided modular dissection of the phage tail fiber protein SGNH55. By decoupling its catalytic and host-binding domains, we generated two highly stable tools: a potent enzyme to eradicate multidrug-resistant biofilms and a sensitive diagnostic probe for rapid pathogen detection. This dual-utility approach provides an innovative therapeutic-diagnostic strategy and establishes a universal framework for engineering complex phage proteins.

papers.title: A nationwide study of pathogens in hospitalized patients with lower respiratory tract infections by metagenomic next-generation sequencing.
papers.abstract: Lower respiratory tract infections remain a major cause of morbidity and mortality, yet timely etiologic diagnosis is difficult because of the breadth of possible pathogens and the limitations of conventional microbiological tests. We retrospectively analyzed 30,819 clinical specimens from 27,507 hospitalized patients with lower respiratory tract infections across 31 provincial-level regions in mainland China from April 2019 to May 2025 to characterize the pathogen spectrum detected by metagenomic sequencing. In total, 323 pathogens were identified, 33.74% of which were fastidious or unculturable microorganisms. The overall positivity rate was 80.12%, and 65.48% of positive specimens showed co-detections. The top 20, 50, 100, 150, and 200 pathogens accounted for 70.17%, 87.56%, 95.59%, 98.18%, and 99.26% of all reported pathogens, respectively. Pathogen distributions differed by age, season, geography, clinical department, and comorbidity, and several epidemiological shifts were observed across the pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-restriction periods, including persistent declines in Streptococcus pneumoniae and Chlamydia psittaci . These findings demonstrate the breadth of organisms detected by metagenomic sequencing in routine practice and support its value for broad etiologic assessment of lower respiratory tract infections.IMPORTANCELower respiratory tract infections are frequently managed before the etiologic agent is established because many bacteria, viruses, fungi, and other organisms can produce similar clinical syndromes, and conventional tests do not capture this diversity well. By analyzing more than 30,000 real-world specimens from hospitalized patients across mainland China, this study shows which organisms are most often detected by metagenomic sequencing, how frequently mixed detections occur, and how pathogen patterns vary by age, geography, season, clinical setting, and the 2019 coronavirus disease period. These findings clarify where broad-range sequencing can add value for microbiology, surveillance, and future targeted panel design.

papers.title: An atlas of colonization factors in the mouse gut microbiome reveals phylogenetically structured repertoires and infection-stage-associated variation during Toxoplasma gondii infection in mice.
papers.abstract: Colonization factors (CFs) comprise CF-associated gene families related to microbial establishment, persistence, host interaction, and gut ecological fitness, but their organization and variation in the mouse gut microbiome remain poorly defined. We integrated the Mouse Gut Genome Catalogue and the Mouse Gut Protein Catalogue, clustered at 90% amino acid identity, to define CF repertoires. A total of 79 conserved CF families, comprising over 2.4 million homologs, were identified across 112,951 genomes from 2,824 microbial species. Species-level CF-associated gene profiles exhibited a clear phylogeny-associated pattern and separated microbial species into two groups with distinct genome-scale functional profiles. Across the cecum and small intestine, CF profiles differed among control, acute, and chronic infection groups in dominant CF abundance, diversity, richness, and overall composition. CF profiles were significantly concordant with taxonomic profiles and associated with microbial community variation. Differential abundance analyses identified tissue- and stage-associated CF features. Exploratory machine-learning analyses showed high classification performance across all feature sets in the cecum, with the genus-level model yielding the highest median performance, whereas species- and genus-level taxonomic profiles provided stronger discrimination than CF profiles in the small intestine. This study provides a reference-based atlas of CF-associated gene repertoires and a CF-centered framework relating these repertoires to microbial phylogeny, genome-scale functional profiles, and infection-stage-associated variation in a murine Toxoplasma gondii infection model. CF-associated gene profiles can complement taxonomic and functional descriptions of the mouse gut microbiome, although the biological roles of individual CF-associated genes require experimental validation.IMPORTANCEStudies of the mouse gut microbiome commonly emphasize taxonomic composition, whereas the ecological traits associated with microbial establishment and persistence in the murine intestine remain less well characterized. By profiling CF-associated gene repertoires across control, acute, and chronic infection groups in mice, we show that infection-stage-associated differences in murine gut microbial community structure are accompanied by differences in colonization- and fitness-associated gene profiles. CF composition was associated with microbial community structure and functional potential, and CF-based features captured intestinal-region- and infection-stage-associated variation within this mouse data set. The principal contribution of this study is a reference-based, CF-centered framework that complements conventional taxonomic and functional profiling in murine infection models and provides a foundation for future mechanistic investigations of microbial colonization.

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Protein Language Models for Dual-Target Antimicrobial Peptide Discovery Under Strict Homology Constraints
papers.abstract: The worldwide escalation of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a severe challenge to modern public health, necessitating novel classes of therapeutic agents. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) represent highly promising alternatives to small-molecule antibiotics due to their co-evolutionary resilience and rapid membrane disruption dynamics. However, translating computational AMP leads into clinical drug candidates remains bottlenecked by off-target cytotoxicity, predominantly hemolytic activity against mammalian erythrocytes. Although pretrained foundational protein language models (PLMs) have rapidly advanced molecular property prediction, current architectures frequently isolate antibacterial potency and cytotoxicity into disconnected single-task pipelines or succumb to catastrophic performance drops under strict homology-controlled evaluations. Recently, the Quantitative Mapping of Antimicrobial Peptides (QMAP) benchmark proposed that frozen PLM embeddings show weak linearly accessible features for hemolytic activity (HC50) resulting in poor rank correlation ({rho} < 0.25) on out-of-distribution sequence splits. In this work, we introduce an end-to-end multi-task parameter-efficient transfer learning framework designed to simultaneously optimize antibacterial potency and minimize mammalian cytotoxicity without sequence leakage. Built upon ESM-2 (150M), our architecture incorporates Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) into self-attention projections, fine-tuning approx 0.70% of model weights. To restore gradient interference originating from disparate membrane lysis mechanisms, we implement an adaptive multi-task loss guided by Kendall homoscedastic uncertainty weighting. Evaluated across predefined QMAP benchmark splits enforcing a 60% maximal sequence identity threshold, our joint architecture remarkably outperforms conventional linear probes, tree-based regressors, and frozen foundational models. The framework achieves an E. coli potency rank correlation of {rho} = 0.6132 (r = 0.6816) and successfully elevates hemolytic toxicity correlation to {rho} = 0.5374 (r = 0.5541). To establish real world utility, we deploy the optimized joint network to screen a curated in silico library of 749 de-novo designed peptides, successfully isolating selective cationic-amphipathic candidates possessing Therapeutic Indices (TI = HC50/MIC) up to 144.03 while effectively deprioritizing broadly lytic motifs (TI < 2.0). These findings demonstrate that parameter-efficient adaptation unlocks fine-grained bioactive structural semantics in foundational PLMs, providing an accurate, scalable framework for therapeutic peptide engineering.

papers.title: Genetics and genomics of enteroarthroconidial development in Coccidioides
papers.abstract: The human fungal pathogen Coccidioides causes disease when its infectious spores, enteroarthroconidia, are inhaled from the soil. Spore dispersal depends on the death of a unique developmental form, disjunctor cells, which flank incipient enteroarthroconidia and are unexplored molecularly. Here we used single-cell (sc) RNA-seq to catalog expression across the Coccidioides colony; with gene deletion and protein tagging, we established a role for the pyropoptosis-like cell death pathway in enteroarthroconidial development.

papers.title: Environment-Aware DNA Language Model for Stress-Responsive Genomic Prioritization in Maize
papers.abstract: Abiotic stresses such as heat and drought severely reduce the productivity of major crops including maize, with adverse implications for agricultural sustainability. Despite progress in characterizing stress resilience, identifying genomic regions associated with stress response remains challenging due to complex genotype-by-environment interactions. Genomic Foundation Models (GFMs), inspired by advances in Large Language Models (LLMs), leverage large-scale self-supervised pre-training on DNA sequences to capture regulatory patterns; however, their adaptation to plant stress-response analysis remains underexplored. In this work, we propose an environment-aware DNA-LLM framework that incorporates stress-specific prompt tokens into AgroNT, a transformer-based plant GFM, using parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT). The model learns stress-conditioned genomic representations that exhibit distinct structures across environmental contexts. We further formulate a prioritization method that uses stress-induced shifts in these representations relative to the control condition together with stress-token-associated transformer attention patterns to identify putative stress-responsive genomic regions. The framework was evaluated on the Genomes-to-Fields (G2F) dataset, comprising over 4,000 maize hybrids grown across 38 locations over 8 years, using grain yield under heat, drought, and combined heat-drought stress. Flowering traits were used to assess generalizability of the stress-conditioned representations across phenotypes. The prioritized regions were assessed using spatiotemporal differential gene-expression profiles, stress-associated quantitative trait loci, and transcription-factor characterization. Regulatory motif analysis further revealed stress-associated motifs enriched within the prioritized sequences as well as model-emphasized high-attention regions. Functional annotation of genes proximal to prioritized regions highlighted roles in transcriptional regulation, signaling, and metabolic pathways relevant to abiotic stress adaptation. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the potential of stress-conditioned transformer-based sequence modeling for environment-aware genome-to-phenome analysis in crop improvement.

papers.title: FedEpitope: Parameter-Efficient Federated Protein Language Models for Linear B-Cell Epitope Prediction
papers.abstract: Linear B-cell epitopes are antigenic regions recognised by antibodies that play crucial roles in vaccine development, antibody production, and other therapeutic applications.Their prediction can support peptide-based vaccine candidate screening and diagnostic assay development, but the experimental data required for model development may be distributed across institutions that cannot freely pool their records. We present FedEpitope, a federated framework that adapts the ESM-2 protein language model for peptide-level linear B-cell epitope prediction using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), keeping client-partitioned data local and restricting the communicated trainable model state to approximately 1.11 MB. Simulated benchmarks of FedAvg and FedProx algorithms, evaluated using homology-aware data splits of five biologically heterogeneous, organism-partitioned clients, achieve promising global test performance without centralising training data, with FedAvg outperforming all single-client models in mean AP, F1, and MCC. Additional experiments characterise post-federation personalisation, record-level differential privacy, sensitivity to controlled client heterogeneity, LoRA rank, and generalisation to the independent BCPreds and NetBCE benchmarks, demonstrating the feasibility of parameter-efficient federated protein language model adaptation for data-localised B-cell epitope prediction and the associated trade-offs among predictive performance, personalisation, privacy, communication efficiency, and distribution shift.

papers.title: Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models
papers.abstract: Recent advances in protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure prediction frameworks have the potential to accelerate computational drug discovery. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond their training sets. Mutation-dependent drug responses present a challenge to these methods because there are often large effects from relatively small perturbations. Here, we systematically benchmark diverse mutational effect and drug-target affinity prediction models using deep mutational scanning datasets spanning 11 inhibitor conditions for the MET kinase domain. Across both mutational effect prediction and drug-target affinity tasks, current AI models produce largely ligand-invariant predictions despite experimentally distinct inhibitor-dependent fitness landscapes. Ligand-aware geometric models, including LigandMPNN and LASErMPNN, partially recover experimentally validated resistance-associated hotspots, highlighting the importance of explicitly modeling protein-ligand interactions and local structural flexibility. In contrast, deep learning affinity prediction models underestimate mutation-induced changes in binding affinity. This deficiency likely reflects mutation-invariant structural priors derived from co-folded structure prediction frameworks and the absence of mutation-conditioned supervision in current affinity datasets. Finally, we further extended our analysis to several kinase-inhibitor deep mutational scanning datasets and confirm the overall trends. Our findings suggest that a primary limitation in improving performance on this task lies in the scarcity of mutation-conditioned protein-ligand training data rather than model architecture alone.

papers.title: Simulating the dynamics of gene regulatory systems at cellular scale
papers.abstract: The temporal nature of eukaryotic gene expression is the result of a complex, non-linear, dynamical system of regulatory processes. So far, models of such systems trade realism for tractability by using strict simplifying assumptions. These simplified models are often unfaithful to our biological understanding; however, without such simplifications, analytical solutions become more challenging and these dynamical systems must then be studied through simulation. Here, we explore the question of how this complex web of gene regulatory connections can be faithfully simulated for all tens of thousands of genes that usually define a eukaryotic organism. We present a proof-of-principle model and simulator, GeneRegulatorySystems.jl which is based on a biophysical chemical master equation that overcomes three key restrictions. First, it allows an exact stochastic simulation of fully non-linear gene expression dynamics, including feedback control, to parsimoniously capture cause and effect relationships of gene regulation. Further, it includes a general framework for implementing diverse mechanisms of gene control such as protein mediated degradation, RNAi, and protein complex formation. Finally, it scales realistically to tens of thousands of genes. We achieve this by introducing a domain-specific programming language to aid the design of experimental protocols from small-scale, well-studied, scenarios of gene regulation inspired by dynamical systems biology up to large-scale, single cell omics experiments with interventions. In this way, our framework provides a grammar of in silico experimental design that can capture single-cell gene expression dynamics for entire genomes.

papers.title: Deep-intronic variants in USH2A: the importance of model selection in variant interpretation and pathogenicity assessment
papers.abstract: Interpreting splice-altering USH2A variants is challenging when these result in the alteration of splicing in only a fraction of transcripts. We investigated two deep-intronic USH2A variants from a single case, the inherited variant c.5573-834A>G and the de novo variant c.11047+345A>G, using a minigene splice assay and transcript analysis in patient-derived photoreceptor precursor cells and nasal epithelial cells. The minigene assay revealed the inclusion of a pseudoexon in the presence of the c.11047+345A>G variant, but did not reproduce previously reported aberrant splicing for c.5573-834A>G. In patient-derived cells, c.5573-834A>G resulted in the inclusion of a pseudoexon in part of the transcripts, whereas c.11047+345A>G did not result in detectable levels of aberrantly spliced transcripts. To assess the impact of residual wildtype transcripts on retinal function, we used the previously developed humanized ush2aPE40+M1 knock-in zebrafish model which allows the modeling of the impact of mixed wildtype and pseudoexon-containing ush2a transcripts. This model demonstrated that detectable levels of usherin expression are maintained even when only a fraction of wildtype transcripts lacking pseudoexon inclusion remain. Collectively, these findings advocate for a more nuanced classification of partially splice-altering USH2A variants. The mere presence of alternative transcripts should not be considered sufficient evidence for pathogenicity. Within this framework, data on the c.5573-834A>G variant do not support a (likely) pathogenic classification, and findings related to the c.11047+345A>G variant are consistent with a likely benign classification.

papers.title: AI-Guided Structure-Aware Modeling and Thermal Proteomics Reveal Direct Demethylzeylasteral-ACLY Interaction
papers.abstract: Identifying the direct molecular targets of bioactive natural products remains a central challenge in chemical biology. Here we present an integrated experimental-computational framework, that combines matrix-augmented thermal proteomics with HoloGNN, a holistic graph neural network, to systematically prioritize and validate protein-ligand interactions. Benchmarking with PDBbind datasets HoloGNN achieves state-of-the-art performance. Applying this framework to 50 structurally diverse natural products identified Demethylzeylasteral as a direct interactor of ACLY. Orthogonal biochemical assays confirmed micromolar binding and enzymatic inhibition. In an imiquimod-induced psoriasis-like mouse model, Demethylzeylasteral reduced disease severity and inflammatory cytokine expression. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed that Demethylzeylasteral reverses keratinocyte hyperproliferation and suppresses ACLY-dependent lipid metabolic reprogramming. Together, this scalable, closed-loop strategy integrates thermal proteomics and machine learning to uncover direct targets of natural products and provides mechanistic evidence linking ACLY inhibition to therapeutic modulation of inflammatory pathology.

papers.title: Agentic Discovery Transfer Enables Cross-Cancer Discovery at Scale
papers.abstract: Cancer research generates tens of thousands of studies each year, yet whether a published finding holds in another cancer type or patient population is rarely tested as doing so is labor-intensive and difficult to scale. We define this task as discovery transfer and present SMART, a multi-agent large language model framework for discovery transfer in single-cell RNA-sequencing studies. Given a source manuscript and a target dataset, SMART extracts major clinical and mechanistic findings, generates and executes analyses for the testable findings, reports which findings transfer, and suggests follow-up. Applied to 121 studies across six cancer types, SMART identified findings that transfer across cancers, including a lung cancer prognostic signature that we confirmed to be associated with survival in liver cancer, pancreatic cancer and pleural mesothelioma. SMART also generated new mechanistic hypotheses, demonstrating how agentic discovery transfer can extend published findings beyond their original setting.

papers.title: Benchmarking DNA Foundation Models: Biological Blind Spots in Evo2 Variant-Effect Prediction
papers.abstract: DNA foundation models such as Evo2 and DNABERT-2 show promise for variant-effect prediction (VEP), yet rigorous benchmarks assessing their ability to capture established biological constraints remain limited. Here, we introduce controlled benchmarks based on well-characterized nuclear and mitochondrial sequence features. Although Evo2 achieves strong aggregate performance on mitochondrial variants (AUROC = 0.927), our analyses reveal systematic blind spots in short-range signals, including codon usage bias, as well as spurious sensitivity to biologically neutral sequence context. Notably, changes in flanking sequences can cause pathogenic tRNA variants to be misclassified as benign. These findings suggest that Evo2's predictive performance may rely more heavily on learned sequence regularities than on the biological constraints governing variant function, raising concerns about the clinical utility of zero-shot genomic foundation models.Our framework provides a principled basis for standardized model evaluation and for guiding the development of architectures better aligned with biological constraints.

papers.title: BioResearchBench: 50 Long Horizon Biological Research Tasks
papers.abstract: AI models are used in biology research to study disease mechanisms, discover potential treatments, analyze experimental data, troubleshoot problems, and plan next steps. Useful assistance depends on working with data in various scientific formats, interpreting results, and deciding what to test next. We present BioResearchBench, a benchmark of 50 research questions developed by PhD biologists drawing on their deep research expertise to reflect realistic problems encountered in their fields. Questions were refined through expert review and iterative model testing. The collection spans 10 diverse biology subdomains and includes sequencing data, proteomic measurements, microscopy images, assay readouts, and clinical datasets. We compared recorded outcomes and examined model responses in depth across the 50 tasks on OpenAI GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, Meta Muse Wonder, and SpaceXSI Grok 4.7. Success across our benchmark was 18% for Claude Opus 5.5, 13% for Gemini 4 Argon, 11% for Meta Muse Wonder, 4% for GPT-6 Astra, and 4% for Grok 4.7. These results describe a deliberately challenging collection selected through expert review and model testing. Despite low whole task success, the selected responses met most rubric requirements on average: the average fraction of criteria missed ranged from 18% to 32% across models. Across models, the proportion of eligible tasks with at least one category failure was highest in computation and data handling (66.9% failure), followed by uncertainty and identification (55.3% failure), reporting and completeness (54.7% failure), biological interpretation (39.0% failure), controls and causal claims (37.2% failure), and choosing the next experiment or decision (31.0% failure). Gemini 4 Argon had the highest proportion of reviewed tasks without a recorded category failure in computation and data handling (45% success) and biological interpretation (69% success). Claude Opus 5.5 led in controls and causal claims (72% success) and choosing the next experiment or decision (75% success). GPT-6 Astra led in uncertainty and identification (56% success) which included judging the precision of estimates and recognizing when measurements could not distinguish between biological explanations. GPT-6 Astra and Meta Muse Wonder tied for the highest proportion of answers with no recorded omissions or reporting failures (51% success). Five case studies presented here show how top AI models can perform many analytical steps correctly yet misinterpret what results signify. For example, some answers described cells as fully recovered when oxygen consumption improved even though mitochondrial membrane potential and cell number remained below control levels. These model answers therefore overstated the extent of cell recovery. Other answers incorrectly called a protein a direct microRNA target, although the experiment had not tested whether the microRNA acted directly on its mRNA or affected it through another process. In a protein turnover task, some model answers misestimated protein half-lives because they did not account for the gradual labeling of amino acids used to make new proteins. These model errors can lead researchers to pursue the wrong explanation even when individual analytical steps are completed correctly. This matters for major scientific goals such as drug discovery, where progress depends on choosing useful experiments and tools, interpreting unexpected results, troubleshooting failed approaches, and deciding which direction is most worth pursuing. Evaluating AI research assistance therefore requires checking whether its explanations, conclusions, and proposed experiments follow from the data and experimental design. These cases highlight continuing challenges in scientific reasoning for frontier AI models: bringing together different types of biological data, analyzing them with appropriate tools and databases, and using the results to draw appropriate conclusions and guide the next steps in research. The observed errors suggest training priorities in data analysis, biological interpretation, and experimental judgment and motivate evaluations that follow researchers and models through iterative scientific work.

papers.title: A comparison of two culture and three sequencing methods for detection of the urobiome
papers.abstract: Standard urine culture (SUC), the clinical reference method, is optimized for fast-growing aerobes and misses much of the urinary microbiota. Enhanced culture and sequencing methods have rarely been compared on the same specimens. We compared five methods (SUC, expanded quantitative urine culture [EQUC], short-read V4 16S rRNA gene sequencing, long-read near full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and PCR-free long-read shotgun metagenomic sequencing) on parallel aliquots of urine from pregnant participants screened for asymptomatic bacteriuria. Of 98 cultured samples, 98 (100.0%) were EQUC-positive while 85 (86.7%) SUC-positive. EQUC detected 102 species, but SUC only detected 41. Short-read 16S rRNA gene sequencing, long-read 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and shotgun sequencing were positive for 188/188, 186/188 and 139/139 samples, detecting 195, 69 and 528 species, respectively. In the 79 samples positive by EQUC and all three sequencing methods, sequencing profiles resembled each other more than culture profiles, and SUC captured only a subset of taxa detected by every other method. Shotgun sequencing gave the broadest taxonomic coverage and was the only sequencing method to identify Escherichia coli to the species level. With EQUC, it outperformed both 16S sequencing methods in detecting Gardnerella vaginalis and distinguishing Lactobacillus species, and it resolved six Gardnerella species, three detected by no other method. Long-read 16S rRNA gene sequencing gave the most confident amplicon-based species assignments, whereas culture better recovered Corynebacterium and Staphylococcus species. No single method was best across all endpoints, but long-read shotgun metagenomics provided the broadest species-level view. Method choice should match the research or clinical question; outcome-based studies are needed to establish clinical utility.

papers.title: Bridging Bibliometrics and Biology: A Framework for the Relevance Scoring and Biological Stratification of Scalable MeSH Co-occurrence Networks
papers.abstract: Systematic literature review is often limited by the rigidity of search strings, which often miss non-obvious but highly relevant topics. Controlled vocabularies such as Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) facilitate the review process, but relationships between terms, and their relevance to a hypothesis of interest, are rarely stated explicitly. Presented here is a MeSH term extraction and networking technique, seeded by a single query for Allergic Contact Dermatitis, forming a "themed" network of terms. The resulting co-occurrence network is pruned by an unsupervised consensus of Metropolis-criterion likelihood search strategies, isolating a significant core subgraph and filtering out incidental co-indexing. Symmetrically normalized Article Relevancy Scores (ARS) then evaluate each article against the network's weighted terms across the annotated MEDLINE corpus, correcting for publication volume bias; Mean Relevancy Scoring (MRS) inverts these scores back onto the terms, scoring each MeSH term by the mean ARS of the articles carrying it to measure its specificity to the query. Benchmarked against the expert-curated Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) for Allergic Contact Dermatitis, the network recovered key event terminology and identified highly specific literature that standard retrieval methods overlooked. This data-driven approach quantitatively assesses associated MeSH terminology, extracting biologically relevant concepts and key relationships directly from the underlying structure of the literature. By automating the discovery of these latent connections, the framework provides a reproducible, scalable foundation for understanding the biomedical literary space surrounding a given search string, assisting systematic review creation, mechanistic pathway mapping, and hypothesis generation across biomedical disciplines.

papers.title: VIGAT: VLM-guided gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq
papers.abstract: Summary: Gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq is challenging because genomic regions informative of cell identity can vary across genes and tissues, while broadly accessible regions may provide limited cell-type-discriminative information. We developed VIGAT, a vision-language model (VLM)-guided tool that automates visual interpretation of ATAC coverage plots for adaptive gene activity quantification. VIGAT jointly examines accessibility patterns across multiple marker genes, integrating genomic annotations and biological context to select gene-specific regions enriched for cluster-discriminative signals. Selected regions are used to generate a gene-by-cell activity matrix. Across 196 paired single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq datasets, VIGAT outperformed five existing methods in recovering marker-associated accessibility enriched in the corresponding cell populations, demonstrating the utility of VLM-guided visual reasoning for scalable gene activity quantification. Availability and implementation: VIGAT is implemented as an open-source R package and is freely available at https://github.com/beijie02/VIGAT.

papers.title: Comprehensive real-world utilization, treatment trajectories, and outcomes of immune checkpoint inhibitors across cancer types: the multicenter FAIR-ICI cohort
papers.abstract: Background: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer treatment, yet evidence on their utilization, treatment trajectories, and effectiveness in routine clinical practice remains limited. We characterized real-world ICI use and outcomes across cancer types using the multicenter FAIR-ICI cohort and explored differences between real-world and pivotal trial outcomes. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults receiving ICIs across four Belgian hospitals. Structured and unstructured electronic health record data were harmonized using the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP-CDM) and natural language processing. We evaluated overall survival (OS), time on treatment (ToT), time to next treatment (TTNT), ICI discontinuation (>12-week treatment gap without re-initiation), and post-discontinuation survival. OS was descriptively compared with pivotal trials, and prognostic factors were assessed using multivariable Cox regression. An interactive public dashboard was developed to enable exploration of cohort characteristics, treatment patterns, and outcomes. Results: Among 3,231 ICI-treated patients, 2,514 (77.8%) had metastatic disease. Among metastatic patients, 568 (22.6%) discontinued ICI without subsequent systemic therapy. Median post-discontinuation OS was 21.4 months (95% CI 16.5-37.2), with 49.1% alive at 24 months. ToT and TTNT were generally shorter than OS, particularly in melanoma (median OS 78 months; ToT 7 months; TTNT 26 months). Real-world survival was frequently less favorable than in pivotal trials. ECOG >=2 was associated with poorer OS than ECOG 0-1 (adjusted HR 2.18, 95% CI 1.82-2.60). In NSCLC patients receiving pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy, survival with ECOG 0-1 more closely approximated trial outcomes, whereas survival with ECOG >=2 was substantially poorer. Conclusions: Real-world ICI treatment trajectories extend beyond active treatment, with some patients experiencing prolonged survival after discontinuation. Differences between real-world and trial outcomes highlight the importance of patient characteristics, particularly performance status, when interpreting trial evidence in routine care. FAIR-ICI provides a scalable framework for evaluating real-world immunotherapy effectiveness, treatment trajectories, and future investigations of treatment-related toxicity.

papers.title: Variant Classification of a Non-Protein Coding Gene: ACMG/AMP Specifications for RMRP from the Clinical Genome Resource Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease Variant Curation Expert Panel
papers.abstract: Purpose: This study, conducted by the Clinical Genome Resource Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease Variant Curation Expert Panel (ClinGen SCID-VCEP), aimed to adapt the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) framework for germline variant interpretation in RMRP. Unlike the protein-coding genes for which the framework was primarily developed, RMRP encodes a non-protein-coding RNA. Biallelic pathogenic variants in RMRP cause cartilage-hair hypoplasia, which can include severe combined immunodeficiency disease and other immune abnormalities. Methods: An RMRP-focused SCID-VCEP subgroup reviewed all 28 ACMG/AMP evidence criteria using population databases, published clinical and experimental data, computational predictions, and expert consensus. Each criterion was retained, modified, or designated as not applicable based on RMRP biology and disease mechanisms. The resulting specifications were pilot tested using 27 variants selected from ClinVar and research laboratory data. Results: Fifteen ACMG/AMP criteria were determined to be applicable to RMRP, while 13 were considered not applicable. Several criteria were modified to evaluate nucleotide-level effects on transcriptional regulation, critical promoter regions, and RNA secondary structure. The specifications also incorporated RMRP-specific recommendations for population frequency, functional evidence, variant phase, segregation, and phenotype. Application of the specifications classified 6 variants as pathogenic, 10 as likely pathogenic, 7 as variants of uncertain significance, and 4 as benign. Previously pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants remained within the pathogenic spectrum, and all previously benign variants remained benign. Variants with conflicting ClinVar interpretations were resolved as either likely pathogenic or uncertain. PM1, PM3, and PP4 were the primary criteria supporting pathogenic classifications. Conclusion: The SCID-VCEP specifications provide a standardized approach to the classification of germline RMRP variants in cartilage-hair hypoplasia and demonstrate how the ACMG/AMP framework can be adapted for a disease-associated non-protein-coding RNA gene. These specifications support the development of variant interpretation frameworks for other clinically relevant non-protein-coding genes.

papers.title: Culture-free Helicobacter pylori genomics reveals within-host virulence heterogeneity and antibiotic resistance
papers.abstract: Helicobacter pylori (Hp) infects over 40% of the world population and causes most cases of gastric cancer worldwide, yet fundamental questions about its within-host genetic diversity remain unresolved. Decades of work on Hp genomics depends on culturing clinical isolates, which can distort within-host genetic heterogeneity that informs Hp virulence and antimicrobial resistance. Culture-free alternatives have been limited by the extremely low Hp abundance in gastric tissue (usually 10^-3 to 10^-7 of total genomic DNA), making direct metagenomics prohibitively expensive and existing enrichment strategies insufficient for whole-genome recovery. Here we develop ultra-sensitive Hp sequencing (uHp-seq) for reconstructing Hp genomes directly from gastric biopsies. uHp-seq achieves a thousand-fold Hp DNA enrichment and recovers near-complete genomes across samples spanning orders of magnitude in Hp abundance. Notably, individual hosts may harbor multiple co-existing Hp strains or cagA EPIYA variants with different oncogenic potential. Resistance-associated variants for six commonly used antibiotics are resolved with greater accuracy than PCR-based and probe-based commercial panels. Applied to minimally invasive gastric string samples, uHp-seq delivers reliable resistance profiles without endoscopy, opening a path to genome-guided Hp eradication.

papers.title: A Knowledge Database of Physical Activity Interventions for Hypertension using Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Physical exercise lowers blood pressure, but guidelines provide broad recommendations that rarely account for age, comorbidities, medications and hypertension severity. A structured, queryable resource of exercise interventions for hypertension is lacking, while manual curation is labor-intensive and difficult to scale. We present PAHD (Physical Activity for Hypertension Database), built with large language models (LLMs). An LLM screened 2,548 PubMed records through title-and-abstract and full-text assessment, selecting 255 studies. LLMs extracted arms, exercise protocols, participant characteristics, and outcomes, with two LLMs cross-checking study structure and each value linked to a verbatim quote. Programmatic integration generated 17,273 standardized records from 253 studies, one per reported comparison. Against adjudicated benchmarks, screening achieved 86.3% recall and 80.6% precision, and extraction 90.1% recall and 90.5% precision for blood pressure values. A clinician-facing portal retrieves studies matched to patients' hypertension stage and comorbidities. PAHD is a reusable, traceable evidence resource for personalized exercise interventions in hypertension.

papers.title: Design and Validation of Multiplexed Respiratory RT-LAMP assay for the differentiation of SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) in COVID-19 Pandemic Samples from Western Kenya.
papers.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the importance of widespread, accessible viral surveillance to ensure pandemic-preparedness. The rapid diagnosis of respiratory infections is crucial not only for effective patient management but also to inform ongoing surveillance for the detection of outbreaks. Reverse transcriptase-Loop mediated isothermal amplification (RT-LAMP) assays are an attractive alternative to reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) for rapid, decentralised testing in resource limited settings due being rapid and low cost. Here we present the design and evaluation of a multiplexed RT-LAMP assay for the simultaneous detection of SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and Respiratory Syncytial Virus via the incorporation of fluorescently labelled LAMP probes. Mid-nasal swabs collected from 175 participants on the day of enrolment in the MALCOV Cohort study in Kisumu, Kenya were used in the evaluation of the RT-LAMP assay. Overall, 114 SARS-CoV-2, six Influenza A, two Influenza B and zero RSV samples were identified in the cohort by the Allplex SARS-CoV-2/FluA/FluB/RSV RT-PCR kit (Seegene Inc) reference test, in addition to 53 negatives. Sensitivity and specificity of the RT-LAMP assay (SARS-CoV-2/FluA/RSV) when compared to RT-PCR was 82.64% [CI95%:74.70-88.92%] and 100% [CI95%:93.40-100%] at 40 minutes for all samples respectively. The mean time to a positive result was 11minutes, highlighting the speed of this technology compared to the more commonly used RT-PCR. RT-LAMP enables rapid multi-pathogen detection with comparable diagnostic accuracy to RT-PCR.

papers.title: DB-ATRG: The Density and BI-RADS-Aware Triage and Automatic Report Generation System for Mammography
papers.abstract: Background: The growing volume of mammography screenings has created severe radiologist shortages, while standard First-In, First-Out (FIFO) reading queues fail to prioritize urgent or complex cases, delaying critical diagnoses.
